The playback method and the permanent saving of an episode are separate choices.

Guidance Notes For the Optimum Listening Experience.

There are several options we recommend that you consider changing. These settings can provide more reliable access to podcast chapters, bookmarks and saved playback positions.

The recommended arrangement is:

  • Allow Leasey to create temporary playback copies.
  • Enable automatic resuming of saved positions.
  • Choose a suitable minimum file length for automatic resuming.

With these settings enabled, you can press Enter on a podcast episode and Leasey will create a temporary playback copy, play it automatically and return to your saved position when you listen again.

Step 1. Open Options by pressing Control+Comma. You are focused upon the General tab.

Step 2. Press the Tab key repeatedly until you reach the Check Box entitled “Resume saved position automatically”.

Step 3. If the Check Box is not already checked, press Space Bar to check it.

When this option is checked, Leasey remembers where you stopped listening to supported audio files.

If you have partly played a podcast episode, pressing Enter on that episode again can resume playback from the saved position rather than starting at the beginning.

For example, suppose you listen to 25 minutes of a one-hour podcast and then stop playback. When you return to the episode later and press Enter, Leasey can begin playing from approximately the 25-minute position.

The saved position belongs to the episode. It does not depend upon you creating a bookmark manually.

Step 4. Press Tab once to reach the Combo Box entitled “Only resume files longer than”.

Step 5. This Combo Box controls the shortest file length for which Leasey will automatically resume playback.

For example, if the setting is 5 minutes, Leasey automatically resumes saved positions only for files longer than 5 minutes.

This prevents short audio files, such as songs, station jingles or brief sound recordings, from unexpectedly beginning part way through. At the same time, longer material such as podcasts, audio books, radio programmes and lectures can resume conveniently.

Use Up Arrow or Down Arrow to change the setting.

A value of 5 minutes should be suitable for most users. However, you may prefer a different value depending upon the kinds of audio files you play.

Step 6. Press Control+Shift+3 to move to the Podcasts tab.

Step 7. Press the Tab key until you reach the Check Box entitled “Use temporary playback copies”.

This option is unchecked by default.

Step 8. Press Space Bar to check the box.

When this option is checked, pressing Enter on a podcast episode causes Leasey to download the episode into its temporary listening area. Leasey then plays the temporary playback copy automatically.

The temporary copy can make the following features more reliable:

  • Podcast chapters.
  • Bookmarks.
  • Saved playback positions.
  • Automatic resuming.
  • Movement through the episode.
  • Continued playback after the initial download has completed.

Unless you have a specific reason to stream episodes directly from the internet, we strongly recommend checking this box.

In most cases, creating the temporary playback copy adds only a short delay between pressing Enter and hearing the episode. The precise time depends upon:

  • The length of the episode.
  • The size of the audio file.
  • The speed of your internet connection.
  • The speed of the podcast provider’s server.
  • Whether a temporary copy of the episode already exists.

Although the delay is often only a few seconds, longer episodes or slower internet connections may take more time.

Leasey should indicate that the episode is being prepared for playback. Once the temporary copy is ready, playback begins automatically.

Temporary playback copies are removed automatically after seven days. They are not placed in your Saved podcast folder and should not be regarded as episodes you have chosen to keep.

Step 9. If you prefer Leasey to stream episodes directly from the internet, press Space Bar to uncheck “Use temporary playback copies”.

When this option is unchecked, pressing Enter on an episode attempts to stream it from the podcast provider.

Control+Shift+K can be used to attempt to resume a streamed episode from its saved position. However, successful resuming depends upon the podcast provider and the way in which the audio is delivered.

Leasey may not always be able to resume streamed content accurately. For this reason, creating temporary playback copies is the recommended method.

Step 10. Press Tab repeatedly until you reach the “OK” Button, then press Enter or Space to save your changes and close Options.

Browsing Feeds and Listening to Podcast Episodes.

The Podcasts screen contains your subscribed podcast feeds. Opening a feed displays the episodes currently available from that podcast provider.

The following procedure explains how to browse your feeds, examine the available episodes and begin playback.

Step 1. From the Podcasts screen, press Control+L to move focus to the list of podcast feeds.

Step 2. Use Up Arrow and Down Arrow to move through the feeds.

As you move through the list, Leasey may announce whether the focused feed contains new episodes.

The information Leasey announces can include:

  • The name of the podcast feed.
  • The number of available episodes.
  • Whether new episodes have been detected.
  • The number of new episodes.

Step 3. To open the focused feed, press Enter.

Step 4. Leasey displays the list of episodes available from that feed.

Step 5. Use Up Arrow and Down Arrow to move through the episodes.

As you move through the episode list, Leasey may identify episodes which have not previously been marked as played.

For example, JAWS might say:

New episode, NPR News: 05-01-2026 7AM EDT, 01 May 2026`

The exact information announced depends upon the title and publication information supplied by the podcast provider.

Filtering the Episode List.

The Episode filter Combo Box appears immediately before the episode list in the tab order.

Step 1. From the episode list, press Shift+Tab to move to the Episode filter Combo Box.

Step 2. Use Up Arrow or Down Arrow to choose which episodes should be displayed.

The available choices are:

  • All episodes.

  • Played episodes.

  • Unplayed episodes.

  • In progress episodes.

  • The filters work as follows.

  • All episodes displays every episode currently available from the open feed.

  • Played episodes displays episodes which have been marked as played.

  • Unplayed episodes displays episodes which have not been marked as played.

In progress episodes displays episodes which have a saved playback position but have not yet been completed.

You can also change the filter using the following keyboard shortcuts:

  • Control+1 displays all episodes.
  • Control+2 displays played episodes.
  • Control+3 displays unplayed episodes.
  • Control+4 displays episodes in progress.

These shortcuts can be used while you are working within an open podcast feed.

For example, if you want to find an episode you started previously but did not finish, press Control+4 to display episodes in progress.

Changing an Episode’s Played Status.

You can manually mark an episode as played or unplayed.

This may be helpful if:

  • You listened to the episode using another device.
  • You do not intend to listen to the episode.
  • An episode has been incorrectly marked.
  • You want an old episode to appear in the unplayed list again.

Step 1. Focus upon the required episode.

Step 2. Open the context menu by pressing the Applications key or Shift+F10.

The context menu contains only commands which are appropriate for the focused episode.

For example, if an episode is already marked as played, the command “Mark as played” is not displayed. Instead, the menu may contain “Mark as unplayed”.

Depending upon the state of the episode, the context menu can include:

  • Mark as played.
  • Mark as unplayed.
  • Save Episode Permanently.
  • Clear saved position.

Step 3. Use Up Arrow or Down Arrow to choose the required command, then press Enter.

Saving an Episode From the Context Menu.

The context menu contains the command “Save Episode Permanently”.

This command always expresses the same intention: you want Leasey to place the episode in your Saved podcast folder and keep it there.

However, Leasey may perform the operation differently depending upon whether a temporary playback copy already exists.

If a temporary playback copy exists, Leasey copies it into your Saved podcast folder. It is not necessary to download the complete episode again.

If there is no temporary playback copy, Leasey downloads the episode from the podcast provider and places it in your Saved podcast folder.

In both cases, the result is the same: the episode becomes a permanently saved file.

When saving an existing temporary playback copy, Leasey also preserves any supported information associated with it, including:

  • Bookmarks you created while listening.
  • The saved playback position.
  • Information which allows you to continue listening from where you stopped.

This means you can begin listening to an episode as a temporary playback copy, create bookmarks or stop part way through, and later decide to save it permanently without losing your listening information.

Leasey creates a subfolder named after the podcast feed if one does not already exist.

Clearing a Saved Position.

The context menu can also contain the command “Clear saved position”.

This command removes the recorded stopping point for the focused episode.

For example, suppose you listened to 20 minutes of an episode and then stopped. Leasey records the 20-minute position.

If you choose “Clear saved position”, that position is reset. The next time you play the episode, playback begins at the start.

Clearing the saved position does not:

  • Delete the episode.
  • Delete a temporary playback copy.
  • Delete a permanently saved episode.
  • Change whether the episode is marked as played.
  • Remove bookmarks.

It removes only the position from which Leasey would otherwise attempt to resume playback.

Reading the Show Notes.

The Show notes Edit Field follows the episode list in the tab order.

Show notes are supplied by the podcast provider and may contain:

  • A description of the episode.
  • The names of guests or presenters.
  • A list of topics.
  • Chapter information.
  • Website addresses.
  • Links to articles or other resources.
  • Contact information.
  • Credits or copyright information.

Step 1. Focus upon an episode in the list.

Step 2. Press Tab once to move to the Show notes Edit Field.

Step 3. Use the standard JAWS reading commands to read the information.

Some show notes may contain website addresses or links which are easier to use in a web browser.

To open the show notes in your default web browser, press Alt+B.

Alternatively, press Tab until you reach the “Show Notes in Browser” Button, then press Enter or Space.

Opening the show notes in a browser can be particularly helpful when you want to:

  • Follow links mentioned in the episode.
  • Download a document.
  • Visit the podcast’s website.
  • Find contact details.
  • Read lengthy notes using web-page navigation commands.
Playing an Episode.

Step 1. Return to the episode list if necessary.

Step 2. Use Up Arrow or Down Arrow to focus upon the episode you want to hear.

Step 3. Press Enter.

What happens next depends upon the setting “Use temporary playback copies”.

If the option is checked, Leasey prepares a temporary playback copy and then plays it automatically.

If the option is unchecked, Leasey attempts to stream the episode directly from the internet.

If automatic resuming is enabled and the episode has a saved position, Leasey attempts to continue from that position.

Player Information.

Press Control+I from the Leasey Media Player window to open a reviewable information window for the current item.

The information can include:

  • The episode title.
  • The podcast name.
  • The current playback position.
  • The total duration, where known.
  • The time remaining, where known.
  • The current playback speed.
  • Whether the item is streaming or local.
  • Whether a podcast episode has been saved permanently.
  • The number of bookmarks.
  • Bookmark names, if bookmarks exist.
  • Whether automatic resume playback is enabled.

The information is displayed in an Edit Field so it can be reviewed with normal JAWS reading commands.

Checking Feeds for New Episodes.

When you enter the Podcasts area of Leasey Media Centre, Leasey checks each feed in your podcast list for new content.

This process can take some time. The amount of time depends upon:

  • The number of feeds in your list.
  • The speed of your internet connection.
  • The response speed of each podcast provider.
  • Whether a feed is temporarily unavailable.
  • The number of new episodes being processed.

You can begin moving through the podcast list while this check is taking place. However, the reported number of new episodes may not yet be complete.

For example, Leasey may initially report that a feed contains no new episodes. A few moments later, once the provider has responded, Leasey may discover that new episodes are available.

For this reason, information announced before the feed check has finished should be regarded as provisional.

When the complete check has finished, JAWS announces the total number of new episodes and the number of feeds in which they were found.

Saving Podcast Episodes Permanently.

You may want to keep a podcast episode permanently on your computer.

This is particularly useful if:

  • You want to listen using another media player.
  • You want to listen without an internet connection.
  • You want to copy the episode to another device.
  • You want to keep an important programme or interview.
  • You want to prevent the episode being lost if the provider removes it.
  • You want the episode to remain available after Leasey removes its temporary playback copy.

A permanently saved episode is placed in your Saved podcast folder. It remains there until you delete or move it.

Saving the Focused Episode.

Step 1. Focus upon the episode you want to save.

Step 2. Press Alt+F to activate the Save Episode Permanently command.

Leasey begins saving the episode.

If a temporary playback copy already exists, Leasey can use that copy rather than downloading the entire episode again.

If no temporary playback copy exists, Leasey downloads the episode from the podcast provider.

Step 3. JAWS should announce that the saving process has started.

Step 4. When the operation is complete, JAWS should announce that the episode has been saved.

If the operation cannot be completed, Leasey should indicate that the save failed.

Possible reasons for failure can include:

  • The internet connection was interrupted.
  • The podcast provider’s server did not respond.
  • The episode is no longer available.
  • The Saved podcast folder cannot be accessed.
  • There is insufficient free disk space.
  • Windows has denied permission to write to the selected folder.

= Security software has prevented the file from being created.

Leasey creates a subfolder named after the podcast feed so that episodes from each podcast are kept together.

For example, if the Saved podcast folder is:

`Podcast Downloads`

and the feed is called:

`Access On`

episodes from that feed are placed in:

`Podcast Downloads\Access On`

Saving an Episode From the Context Menu.

You can also save an episode using its context menu.

Step 1. Focus upon the required episode.

Step 2. Press the Applications key or Shift+F10.

Step 3. Use Up Arrow or Down Arrow to find “Save Episode Permanently”.

Step 4. Press Enter.

The result is the same as pressing Alt+F. The episode is placed in your Saved podcast folder and retained permanently.

Choosing the Saved Podcast Folder.

The Saved podcast folder determines where permanently saved podcast episodes are stored.

Changing this folder does not change the location used for temporary playback copies. Temporary files continue to be managed separately by Leasey.

Step 1. Press Control+Comma to open Options.

Step 2. Press Control+Shift+3 to move to the Podcasts tab.

Step 3. Press Tab until you reach the Edit Field entitled “Saved podcast folder”.

This Edit Field contains the full path to the folder in which permanently saved podcast episodes will be stored.

You can type or paste a folder path directly into the Edit Field.

For example:

`C:\Users\YourName\Documents\Podcast Downloads`

You can also use the Browse Button to select a folder using standard Windows techniques.

Step 4. To use the Browse Button, press Tab once from the Saved podcast folder Edit Field.

Step 5. Press Enter or Space to activate the Browse Button.

Step 6. Choose the required folder and confirm your selection.

The selected folder path is placed in the Saved podcast folder Edit Field.

Step 7. Press Tab repeatedly until you reach the “OK” Button.

Step 8. Press Enter or Space to save the setting and close Options.

Future episodes which you save permanently will be placed in the selected folder.

Changing the Saved podcast folder does not automatically move episodes which were saved previously. Existing files remain in their original folders unless you move them manually.

Choosing a Suitable Folder.

We recommend choosing a folder which:

  • Is easy for you to locate.
  • Has sufficient free disk space.
  • Is included in your normal backup arrangements, if the episodes are important.
  • Is not a temporary Windows folder.
  • Does not require administrator permission whenever a file is saved.

You may wish to create a folder specifically for Leasey podcast episodes.

For example:

`C:\Users\YourName\Music\Leasey Podcasts`

or:

`D:\Podcast Downloads`

If you use a cloud-synchronised folder, such as one within OneDrive or Dropbox, remember that permanently saved episodes may also be uploaded to the cloud. Podcast audio files can be large and may use a significant amount of storage or internet bandwidth.

Saving Multiple Podcast Episodes.

You may sometimes want to save several episodes from the same podcast feed.

For example, you may want to:

  • Save a short series of programmes.
  • Download several episodes before travelling.
  • Keep a group of interviews.
  • Work through an older podcast from the beginning.
  • Save episodes before they are removed by the provider.

Leasey does not attempt to save every available episode from a feed at once.

Some feeds contain hundreds or even thousands of episodes. Saving all of them could:

  • Take a very long time.
  • Use a large amount of disk space.
  • Consume considerable internet bandwidth.
  • Place excessive demand upon the podcast provider’s server.
  • Make it difficult to identify which episodes you intended to keep.

Instead, Leasey divides the available episodes into manageable ranges of ten.

Selecting a Range of Episodes.

Step 1. Open the required podcast feed.

Step 2. Press Tab until you reach the “Save Multiple Episodes” Button.

Step 3. Press Enter or Space.

A Dialog Box opens containing a list of episode ranges.

The ranges are presented in listening order, from oldest to newest.

For example, you may hear:

  • Episodes 1 to 10.
  • Episodes 11 to 20.
  • Episodes 21 to 30.

The first range contains the oldest episodes in the feed.

This arrangement is particularly useful when you want to begin listening to a podcast from its earliest available episode.

Step 4. Use Up Arrow or Down Arrow to choose the required range.

Reviewing the Selected Episodes.

Before beginning the save operation, you can review the episodes contained in the selected range.

Step 1. After choosing a range, press Tab to move to the Edit Field entitled “Selected episodes and save results”.

The Edit Field lists the titles of the episodes in the selected range.

Step 2. Use the standard JAWS reading commands to review the titles.

This allows you to confirm that the range contains the episodes you want before any files are saved.

If the feed contains fewer than ten episodes in the final range, only the remaining episodes are included.

For example, if a feed contains 24 episodes, the ranges may be:

  • Episodes 1 to 10.
  • Episodes 11 to 20.
  • Episodes 21 to 24.
Beginning the Save Operation.

Step 1. Return to the list of episode ranges if necessary.

Step 2. Focus upon the range you want to save.

Step 3. Press Enter.

Alternatively, press Tab until you reach the “Save Selected Range” Button, then press Enter or Space.

Leasey begins processing the selected episodes.

As each episode is handled, the Selected episodes and save results Edit Field is updated.

The results may indicate:

  • Which episode is currently being saved.
  • Which episodes were saved successfully.
  • Which episodes could not be saved.
  • Whether an existing temporary playback copy was used.
  • Whether an episode had to be downloaded from the provider.

When the complete operation has finished, JAWS announces:

  • How many episodes were saved successfully.
  • How many episodes failed, if any.

If one or more episodes fail, the other episodes in the range may still be saved successfully.

A failure does not necessarily mean that the entire operation has failed.

Episodes may fail individually because:

  • A particular episode is no longer available.
  • Its download address is invalid.
  • The provider’s server did not respond.
  • The file could not be written to disk.
  • The internet connection was interrupted.
  • The provider temporarily refused the request.

You can review the results Edit Field to determine which episodes were affected.

File Names and Listening Order.

Permanently saved episodes are numbered as well as named.

The numbering helps to keep the files in the correct listening order when they are viewed in File Explorer or opened in another media player.

This is especially useful when:

  • Episode titles do not begin with a date or episode number.
  • A series should be heard in chronological order.
  • The podcast provider lists the newest episode first.
  • You are saving an older sequence of episodes.

The files are placed in the subfolder belonging to the podcast feed within your Saved podcast folder.

Cancelling Before Saving.

If you change your mind before starting the operation, press Escape to close the Dialog Box.

No episodes are saved if you close the Dialog Box before activating the selected range.

Once the saving process has begun, allow Leasey to finish processing the range.

Summary of Podcast File Terminology.

The following terms are used throughout Leasey Media Centre.

Stream.

To play an episode directly from the podcast provider over the internet.

A complete local copy is not created before playback begins.

Temporary Playback Copy.

A copy which Leasey creates automatically to improve listening.

It can support:

  • Podcast chapters.
  • Bookmarks.
  • Saved playback positions.
  • Automatic resuming.
  • More reliable movement through the episode.

Temporary playback copies are normally removed after seven days.

Saved Episode.

An episode which you have deliberately chosen to keep permanently.

It is placed in your Saved podcast folder and remains there until you move or delete it.

Save Episode Permanently.

A command which places the focused episode in your Saved podcast folder.

If a temporary playback copy already exists, Leasey can use it. Otherwise, Leasey downloads the episode from the podcast provider.

Saved Podcast Folder.

The folder in which permanently saved podcast episodes are stored.

This folder is separate from Leasey’s temporary listening area.

Remember:

Temporary playback copies are created to help you listen. Saved episodes are files you have chosen to keep.

Transcribing Podcast Episodes.

Leasey Media Centre can create a text transcript of a podcast episode. This can be useful if you want to search through an episode, keep written notes from it, review a section more carefully, or copy information from the spoken content. It also assists people who are unable to hear the audio content.

Where possible, the transcript separates different speakers. They are identified as Speaker 1, Speaker 2 and so on. Speaker separation is not always perfect, especially if people talk over each other or the audio quality is poor, but it can be very helpful for interviews and discussion programmes.

Step 1. Open a podcast feed and move to the episode you want to transcribe.

Step 2. Press Tab until you reach the Transcribe episode Button.

Step 3. Press Enter or Space.

Step 4. JAWS should announce that transcription has started. Focus is placed in the show notes Edit Field so you can continue reviewing the episode details while the transcript is being prepared.

Step 5. While the transcript is being prepared, Leasey gives progress messages approximately every 15 seconds. The exact time taken depends upon the length of the episode and the current speed of the transcription process. The average time taken to transcribe a podcast with a duration of one hour is approximately 40 to 50 seconds.

Step 6. When the transcript is ready, a Podcast Transcript window opens. The transcript is in a read-only Edit Field, so you can review it with the arrow keys.

Step 7. If required, Tab to Copy Transcript and press Enter or Space to copy the transcript to the clipboard. You can also Tab to Save Transcript and press Enter or Space to save it as a text file.

Step 8. If you would like a shorter version of the transcript, Tab to Create Summary and press Enter or Space.

Step 9. JAWS should announce that the summary has started. While the summary is being prepared, Leasey gives progress messages approximately every 30 seconds.

Step 10. When the summary is ready, focus is placed in the Summary Edit Field. The summary is presented as plain text, so you can review it with the arrow keys.

Step 11. If required, Tab to Copy Summary and press Enter or Space to copy the summary to the clipboard. You can also Tab to Save Summary and press Enter or Space to save it as a text file. The save dialog for a summary is called Podcast Summary.

Step 12. Press Escape or activate Close when you have finished reviewing the transcript or summary.

Searching For Specific Content.

Suppose you have subscribed to a podcast and you would like to check the feed for specific content. Leasey can search the podcast show notes for key words.

Going back to our Access On podcast, let us discover whether they have anything useful to say about Braille.

Step 1. We have previously subscribed to Access On. Press Control+L to access the list of feeds.

Step 2. Using the Up or Down Arrow keys, locate the Access On podcast and press Enter.

Step 3. Press Control+F.

Step 4. Type the word Braille and press Enter.

Step 5. A list of results is returned containing the term you have requested. At the time of writing, 18 episodes are returned for this feed containing the word Braille.

Step 6. The structure of this Dialog Box is exactly the same as if you were viewing regular feed episodes. You can press Enter to play a podcast episode or press Tab to reach the show notes. You can also download it to the computer by pressing Alt+F.

Checking For New Episodes.

Each time you start Leasey Media Centre in the podcasts area, Leasey will check for new episodes to the feeds you have subscribed to. If new content is found, you will be advised of this. JAWS will announce how many episodes have been found and the number of feeds they relate to.

You can however force a manual refresh.

Step 1. Press Control+L to move to the list of feeds.

Step 2. Press Tab to reach the Check New Episodes Button and press Enter or Space.

Step 3. If new episodes are found, you will be placed in a list of feeds containing new content. Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to find a feed and press Enter to access it.

Chapter Marks.

Some podcast files contain chapter marks.

Chapter marks divide a long audio file into named sections. For example, a podcast might contain chapters for the introduction, an interview, a product review, listener questions and closing comments. This makes it possible to move directly to a particular part of the programme rather than searching through the audio manually.

When a local file contains chapter marks, the player title includes the words “chapters available”. Press JAWS Key+T to read the window title.

If you are playing a podcast from a temporary MP3 playback copy, chapter marks can also be accessed when they are available.

Use Control+Left Arrow and Control+Right Arrow to move backwards and forwards through the chapters.

Press Control+Shift+L to display a list of chapters. Where possible, Leasey obtains the chapter name and start time.

Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to move through the list. When you find the chapter you want to hear, press Enter to move directly to its starting position.

Chapter marks supplied by the podcast producer are read-only. Leasey allows you to move to them, but you cannot rename or delete them.

Creating Chapter Marks Manually.

Leasey can also create chapter marks of its own. If a chapter was created by Leasey in a local MP3 file or temporary MP3 playback copy, it is identified in the chapter list as a Leasey chapter. The words “Leasey chapter” are spoken only within the Leasey chapter list so that you know which chapters can be changed. They are not added to the actual chapter title.

This is particularly useful if you are the producer of a podcast or other MP3 audio file. You can create chapter marks within Leasey and have them written directly into the MP3 metadata. The file can then be distributed or downloaded in the usual way, and the chapter marks can be recognised by other podcast or media players which support MP3 chapter navigation.

To create a Leasey chapter:

Step 1. Play a podcast episode from a temporary MP3 playback copy, or play a local MP3 file.

Step 2. Move to the position where you want the new chapter to begin.

Step 3. Press Control+Shift+H.

Step 4. The Add MP3 Chapter Dialog opens.

Step 5. Type the chapter title.

Step 6. Tab to the Time position Edit Field.

The time position is filled in with the current playback position. You can edit this value if you want the chapter to begin slightly earlier or later.

The time can include tenths of a second. For example:

  • 23.2 means 23.2 seconds.
  • 1:04.5 means 1 minute, 4.5 seconds.
  • 1:04:15.5 means 1 hour, 4 minutes, 15.5 seconds.

Step 7. If you want to check the position before creating the chapter, Tab to Preview and press Enter or Space.

Preview plays briefly from the proposed chapter point and then returns to the original position and pauses.

Step 8. If the chapter point needs fine adjustment, use Move earlier or Move later.

Move earlier moves the proposed chapter point back by a quarter of a second.

Move later moves the proposed chapter point forward by a quarter of a second.

Step 9. When the title and time position are correct, Tab to OK and press Enter or Space.

Before writing the new chapter information into the MP3 file, Leasey creates a backup copy of the file. The new chapter is then shown in the chapter list as a Leasey chapter.

From the chapter list:

  • F2 renames the focused Leasey chapter.
  • Delete removes the focused Leasey chapter.

These commands apply only to chapters created by Leasey. Chapters supplied by the original podcast producer remain read-only.

Creating Chapters Based On Podcast Content.

If a podcast episode does not contain any chapter marks, pressing Control+Shift+L offers to create suggested chapters.

Leasey reviews the podcast transcript and creates topic-based summary chapters. Each suggested chapter includes a description of that section and a time position. These suggested chapters are intended to provide useful structure where no chapter information was supplied by the podcast producer. They should therefore be treated as helpful estimates rather than exact chapter information.

Suggested chapters are not written into the audio file automatically.

When suggested chapters have been created, press Control+Shift+L to open the suggested chapter list.

Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to review the suggested sections. Each item represents a possible section of the podcast. Press Enter on a suggested chapter to move directly to that position in the audio.

You can continue to use the suggested chapters in this temporary form without making any changes to the MP3 file.

If the current episode is being played from a temporary MP3 playback copy the suggested chapter list also contains a “Make Permanent” Button. Press Enter or Space on this Button if you want Leasey to write the suggested chapters permanently into the MP3 file metadata. Once the suggested chapters have been written into the file, they become Leasey chapters. They are then identified as Leasey chapters within the chapter list and can be edited in the same way as chapters you created manually.

  • Press F2 to rename a Leasey chapter. You may wish to do this because the Leasey chapter descriptions are quite lengthy. This is by design in order for you to gain an appreciation of the content in that audio segment.
  • Press Delete to remove a Leasey chapter.

Because the chapters are now stored within the MP3 metadata, they remain with the audio file and can be recognised by other podcast or media players which support MP3 chapter navigation.

If you want to permanently keep a podcast episode with its Leasey chapters, you should do this.

Step 1. Start playing a podcast episode.

Step 2. Pause the audio by pressing Space on the Play/Pause Button in focus.

Step 3. Press Control+Shift+L. Leasey will offer to create the temporary chapters for you. Press Enter or Space on the “Yes” Button which is in focus.

Step 4. Leasey in time will bring back the suggested chapters. If you have already done this once the results will immediately be displayed.

Step 5. Press the Tab key to reach the “Make Permanent” Button and press Enter or Space. The chapter information is written to the file permanently.

Step 6. Press Escape to exit the player.

Step 7. Focus should have returned to the episode list and the correct podcast episode.

Step 8. Press ALT+F to download it.

Step 9. Find that file using File Explorer or Leasey File Manager.

Step 10. Open it up and Leasey will play it.

Step 11. Press Control+Shift+L. Your chapters should be there. Even at that stage, they could be renamed if necessary.

Renaming a Podcast Feed.

The names of podcasts in the feeds list do not need to reflect the podcast titles. They can be whatever you would like them to be.

Step 1. Ensure you are focused within the list of feeds.

Step 2. Move to a feed where you wish to change the name, such as, “My Very Exciting Podcast”.

Step 3. Press F2.

Step 4. Type the new name and press Enter.

Step 5. The new name should be reflected in the feeds list. It will not affect the functionality of listening to or downloading the podcasts.

Obtaining the URL of a Podcast Episode.

You may wish to obtain the URL of a podcast episode, perhaps for submitting to an external service or for sharing with other people.

Step 1. Begin playing the episode for which you wish to obtain the URL.

Step 2. Press Control+E.

Step 3. The URL pointing to the publicly available file is displayed in a read-only Edit Field.

Step 4. You can either copy it from the Edit Field or press the Tab key to reach the Copy Button, then press Enter or Space.

Remembering Speed of Playback.

Under most circumstances, when you adjust speed of playback using the Left and Right Bracket keys, Leasey remembers the speed preference for either podcasts or audio files. However it is possible to remember the speed of playback for a specific item, such as a podcast episode.

Step 1. Start playing the podcast episode.

Step 2. Adjust the speed of playback as required with the Left and Right Bracket keys.

Step 3. Press Control+Shift+Y. This saves the preferred speed of playback for that item.

Should you wish the playback speed to be no longer retained for the podcast episode, press ALT+Control+Y.

Unsubscribing From a Podcast.

If you wish to remove a podcast from your feeds list, do the following:

Step 1. Press Control+L to access the feeds list.

Step 2. Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to find the feed to be removed.

Step 3. Press the Delete key.

Step 4. You will be asked for confirmation of the deletion. Type letter Y for Yes or N for No. You can also press Enter since Yes is the focused control.

Audio and Playlists.

Audio and Playlists is accessed by pressing the Leasey Key then A for Audio, and selecting the first item, Work with Audio and Playlists. When you press this key combination, the Tasks Combo Box previously referred to is automatically set to the Audio and Playlists area. If you are focused in Leasey Media Centre already, you can press Alt+3.

The Audio and Playlists area contains:

  • Playlists list.
  • New playlist Button.
  • Delete playlist Button.
  • Add files Button.
  • Add Folder Button.
  • Remove track Button.
  • Move up Button.
  • Move down Button.
  • Tracks list.
  • Playlist order Combo Box.
  • Open file Button.
  • Open folder Button.
  • Play track Button.
  • Play playlist Button.
  • Edit tags Button.
  • Batch tag editor Button.
  • Audio converter Button.
  • Close Button.
Useful Audio and Playlist Keystrokes.

Control+O opens a streaming URL, local audio file, supported video file soundtrack or playlist.

Supported audio files include:

  • MP3.
  • M4A.
  • M4B.
  • AAC.
  • WAV.
  • FLAC.
  • OGG.
  • OPUS.
  • WMA.

Supported video files, where Leasey Media Centre plays the soundtrack, include:

  • MP4.
  • MKV.
  • M4V.
  • MOV.
  • AVI.
  • WEBM.
  • WMV.
  • 3GP.

Supported playlist files include:

  • M3U.

M3U8 [ PLS.

The keystrokes continue.

  • Alt+P moves to the playlist list.
  • Alt+L moves to the tracks in the playlist.
  • Control+N creates a new playlist.
  • Alt+A adds one or more files to the selected playlist.
  • Alt+F adds a folder to the selected playlist.
  • Open folder plays the contents of a folder temporarily without creating a playlist.
  • Control+Shift+E edits tags for the selected track in the Tracks list.
  • Alt+E opens the Batch Tag Editor from the Audio and Playlists area.
  • Enter on a playlist starts playing it.
  • Enter on a track plays that track.
  • Delete on a track removes it from the playlist.
Opening Audio Files or Streaming URLs.

Control+O opens the Open Media dialog.

This dialog can be used in two different ways.

The first edit field is Streaming URL. Use this field when you have a direct streaming address for an internet radio station or other playable audio stream.

Examples of suitable streaming URLs include:

  • Direct MP3 streams.
  • Direct AAC or AAC Plus streams.
  • Direct OGG or Opus streams.
  • M3U or M3U8 playlist streams where the player can resolve the audio.
  • PLS playlist streams where the player can resolve the audio.

The Streaming URL field is not intended for ordinary web pages. For example, a station home page, a YouTube page, a SoundCloud page, or a page containing an embedded player is not usually a direct streaming URL. If the URL does not play in other media players such as VLC or Winamp, it is unlikely to play here.

To open a streaming URL:

Step 1. Press Control+O.

Step 2. Type or paste the streaming URL into the Streaming URL edit field.

Step 3. Press Enter.

Leasey Media Player opens and attempts to play the stream. The stream is not added to favourites, presets, or the main station directory. This makes the feature useful for testing a stream before deciding whether it should be added permanently.

The second edit field is Audio file. You can reach this by pressing Tab. Use this field when you want to open a local audio file, supported video file soundtrack, or playlist file.

You can type a complete path to a file and press Enter. You can also type part of a path, such as a drive letter or folder, and press Enter. The standard Windows Open dialog appears from that location. Choose the file and press Enter. The selected file starts playing immediately.

When you open a local file, Leasey remembers the folder. The next time you open the Open Media dialog and use the Audio file field to browse, the standard Windows Open dialog starts in the last folder you used.

Supported audio files include MP3, M4A, M4B, AAC, WAV, FLAC, OGG, Opus and WMA. Supported video files for audio playback include MP4, MKV, M4V, MOV, AVI, WebM, WMV and 3GP. Supported playlist files include M3U, M3U8 and PLS.

If both Streaming URL and Audio file contain text, Leasey asks you to use one field or the other.

Playing a Folder Without Creating a Playlist.

You may want to play the contents of a folder without first creating a playlist.

Step 1. Move to Audio and Playlists.

Step 2. Press Tab until you reach the Open folder Button.

Step 3. Press Enter or Space.

Step 4. Choose the folder containing the files you want to play.

Leasey plays the supported audio files and video soundtracks in that folder as a temporary list. This does not create a playlist and does not save the folder as a playlist.

If no supported files are found directly in the folder, Leasey asks whether subfolders should be searched.

If you have registered File Explorer entries from Options, you can also focus a folder in File Explorer, press the Applications key, and choose Play folder with Leasey Media Player.

If you are using Leasey File Manager, you can focus upon the folder containing audio files and press Control+Shift+L for the “Send to Leasey” command. From there, press Down Arrow to reach the item “Play with Leasey Media Player” and press Enter.

Creating a Playlist.

To create a playlist.

Step 1. Press Control+N.

Step 2. Type the playlist name and press Enter.

Step 3. Activate Add files, or press Alt+A, to add one or more audio files or supported video files. This will allow you to browse to the files to add using standard Windows techniques.

Step 4. If you wish to add an entire folder, press Alt+F or activate the Add Folder Button.

Step 5. After choosing the folder, Leasey Media Centre asks whether files in subfolders should also be included. Type Y for Yes or N for No. You can also press Enter since the Yes Button is the focused control. The tracks are shown in the Tracks list.

Step 6. Alternatively, find the file using File Explorer or Leasey File Manager, copy it to the clipboard, focus back on the Playlist Viewer and press Control+V.

Managing Track Order.

You can rearrange the items in the playlist:

Step 1. Move to a track in the Tracks list.

Step 2. Activate Move up or Move down; Alt+U or Alt+D.

JAWS should announce:

Moved Song A below Song B.

Step 3. Multiple files can be selected for deletion or moving by focusing upon each one and pressing the Comma key. JAWS reports that a file is selected. You can verify which files have been selected by:

  • Moving to a file with the arrow keys. JAWS reports if it has been selected.
  • Typing forward slash. JAWS recites all the items which are selected.
  • Should you wish to clear the selection, type full-stop or period.
Listening to a Playlist.

The Playlist order Combo Box allows you to choose:

  • Sequential.
  • Shuffle.
  • Repeat.

Sequential plays the playlist in the displayed order.

Shuffle plays the items in a random order.

Repeat begins the playlist content again when it reaches the end.

You can press Tab or Shift+Tab repeatedly to reach the Combo Box and the Up or Down Arrow keys can be used to change the value.

Creating a Playlist and Listening to It.

We will now create a playlist, add tracks to it and begin listening to it using Leasey Media Player. Note that the Leasey Media Player must be used in order to listen to playlists.

Step 1. Press the Leasey Key followed by letter A for Audio.

Step 2. From the menu which appears, press Enter on the first item, Work with Audio and Playlists.

Step 3. The Audio and Playlists window appears.

Step 4. Press Control+N to create a new playlist.

Step 5. Type the name for the playlist, such as, Oldies. Then press Enter. JAWS confirms that the playlist has been created.

Step 6. We will first add an artist folder and sub-folders. Press Alt+F.

Step 7. Using standard Windows techniques, browse to the folder containing a music artist and press Enter to select it.

Step 8. Tab to the Select Folder Button and press Enter or Space.

Step 9. You are asked if you would like to add sub-folders to the playlist. Type letter Y for Yes or N for No. On this occasion, we will choose Yes by typing the letter Y. JAWS confirms how many files were added. We do not need to be concerned with saving a playlist because it is automatically saved.

Step 10. Close down Leasey Media Centre by pressing Alt+F4. Of course we do not need to do this but it illustrates the next point very well.

Step 11. Load up the Leasey Media Centre once more with the audio and Playlists area in focus. This is achieved by pressing the Leasey Key then letter A and pressing Enter on the first item, Work with Audio and Playlists.

Step 12. Press Alt+P to focus upon your list of playlists.

Step 13. Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to focus upon the name of the playlist.

Step 14. You now have a choice. Pressing Enter will begin playing the playlist in the order specified within the Playlist Order Combo Box. By default this is sequential. If you wish to change this, press Tab or Shift+Tab to reach the Combo Box and then Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to change the value.

Step 15. However, if you only want to hear an individual track from the playlist, press Alt+L to focus upon the list of tracks. Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to move to the desired item and press Enter to play.

Editing Tags for One Audio File.

Leasey Media Centre can edit tags for MP3, M4A, FLAC, OGG and Opus files.

This includes:

  • Title.
  • Artist.
  • Album.
  • Album artist.
  • Track number.
  • Genre.
  • Year/date.
  • Comment.

To edit tags for a track in a playlist:

Step 1. Move to Audio and Playlists.

Step 2. Press Alt+P to focus on the list of playlists.

Step 3. Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to choose the playlist you want.

Step 4. Press Alt+L to focus upon the list of tracks in the playlist.

Step 5. Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to move to the track you want to edit.

Step 6. Press Control+Shift+E, or Tab to the Edit tags Button and press Enter or Space.

Step 7. The Edit Audio Tags dialog opens.

Step 8. The first field is Title. Tab through the fields and make the changes you want.

Step 9. Press Enter or Space on the Save Button to save the tags.

JAWS should announce:

Tags saved.

You can also edit tags for the file which is currently loaded in the Leasey Media Player by pressing Control+E in the player window.

Tag editing is only available for local MP3, M4A, FLAC, OGG and Opus files. It is not available for radio streams, podcast streams, playlist URLs or other audio formats. If the file is playing, you can usually edit the tags without stopping playback. After saving, the player title and spoken track name should update to reflect the new title and artist.

Batch Tag Editor.

The Batch Tag Editor is useful when you want to review or change tags for a group of MP3, M4A, FLAC, OGG or Opus files.

Step 1. Move to Audio and Playlists.

Step 2. Press Alt+E to activate the Batch tag editor.

Step 3. The Batch Tag Editor contains:

  • Folder Edit Field.
  • Load folder Button.
  • Load files Button.
  • Include subfolders Check Box.
  • Files list.
  • Tag Edit Fields for the selected file.
  • Save Button.
  • Save and next Button.
  • Reload Button.
  • Buttons to apply artist, album, album artist, genre or year/date to selected files.
  • Close Button.

To load a folder:

Step 1. Type or paste a folder path into the Edit Field.

Step 2. Alternatively, Tab to the Load Folder Button and press Enter or Space.

Step 3. Using standard Windows navigation techniques, choose the folder containing the files and press Enter.

Step 4. If you want to include files in subfolders, check Include subfolders before loading the folder. You can press the Tab key to reach this Check Box. Press Space to check or uncheck it.

To load specific files:

Step 1. Tab to the Load File Button and press Enter or Space.

Step 2. Using standard Windows navigation techniques, choose the file and press Enter.

The files list shows the loaded files. As you move through the list, JAWS should speak useful information such as the artist and title, where available. The Edit Fields for each file, which you can reach by repeatedly pressing the Tab key, show the tags for the selected file.

To change one file:

Step 1. Move to the file in the list.

Step 2. Tab to the field you want to change.

Step 3. Type the new value.

Step 4. Activate Save, or press Control+S. Focus returns to the files list after saving.

To save and move to the next file:

Step 1. Make the changes you want.

Step 2. Press Tab to reach the Save and Next Button and press Enter or Space.

To apply the same value to several files:

Step 1. Select the files in the list.

Step 2. Type the value into the appropriate field, such as Artist, Album, Album artist, Genre or Year/date.

Step 3. Tab to one of these Buttons depending upon what you are trying to change:

  • Apply artist to selected files.
  • Apply album to selected files.
  • Apply album artist to selected files.
  • Apply genre to selected files.
  • Apply year/date to selected files.

Step 4. Press Enter or Space on the appropriate Button.

Step 5. You will be asked to confirm if more than one file is being changed. Type Y for Yes or N for No. Pressing Enter is possible since Yes is the focused control.

The Batch Tag Editor does not rename files. It does not change album art. It preserves unrelated metadata where possible. If a file is read-only or cannot be updated, a clear error is shown.

Audio Converter.

The Audio Converter is available from the Audio and Playlists area.

You can open it in either of the following ways.

From the main Leasey Media Centre window, press ALT+C.

Alternatively:

Step 1. Press the Leasey Key then A to activate the Leasey Audio Menu.

Step 2. Press End to reach the last item, Audio Converter.

Step 3. Press Enter.

You can also press the Tab key to reach the Audio Converter Button in the Audio and Playlists area, then press Enter or Space.

The first control is the Load Files Button. Pressing Enter on this Button will allow you to browse for files using standard Windows techniques. Press Enter when the file or files are found. Alternatively, Tab to the Load Folder Button and press Enter or Space.

Activating this Button allows you to browse to the folder using standard Windows techniques.

If you load a folder, you can choose whether to include files in subfolders. This is a Check Box. Press the Space Bar to Check or Uncheck it. Press Tab and you should be able to examine the list of files added in the previous steps.

Step 7. Pressing Tab again moves to the Output folder Edit Field. This location should be used to send the converted files. Type or paste a full folder path into this field.

Step 8. Alternatively, press Tab to reach the Browse Button and press Enter or Space. This gives you the opportunity of browsing to an output folder using standard Windows techniques.

If you loaded individual files, the converted files are placed directly in the output folder. If you loaded a folder, Leasey Media Centre creates a folder with the same name inside the output folder, and places the converted files there. For example, if the output folder is Leasey Conversions and the folder being converted is called Lecture Series, the converted files are placed in Leasey Conversions\Lecture Series. If subfolders were included, their structure is preserved inside that folder.

Step 9. Press Tab again to reach the Output format Combo Box.

Step 10. Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to select an output format. The choices are:

  • WAV.
  • MP3 128K.
  • MP3 192K.
  • MP3 320K.
  • FLAC.
  • M4A AAC 192K.
  • OGG Vorbis 192K.

For example, you can convert an M4A file to WAV or a video file to MP3. Leasey Media Centre does not overwrite existing files. If a file with the same name already exists in the output folder, a numbered file name is created.

Step 11. Tab to the Convert Button and press Enter or Space.

If you have registered File Explorer entries from Options, you can also convert one file directly from File Explorer. Focus the audio file in File Explorer, press the Applications key, and choose Convert with Leasey Audio Converter. The Audio Converter opens with that file already loaded. This Explorer command is separate from Play with Leasey Media Centre on the Context Menu and does not change your default audio player.

Send to Leasey from Leasey File Manager.

Leasey File Manager includes a Send to Leasey command.

Press Control+Shift+L to open it.

You can also open the context menu with the Applications key or Shift+F10 and choose Send to Leasey.

For audio files, Send to Leasey can offer:

  • Play with Leasey Media Player.
  • Add to Leasey Media Centre Queue.
  • Tag with Leasey Tag Editor.
  • Convert with Leasey Audio Converter.

The exact choices depend on the file type. For example, MP3, M4A, MP4 and FLAC files can be sent to the tag editor. Common audio files such as MP3, WAV, M4A, FLAC and WMA can be sent to Leasey Media Centre.

If there is no suitable Leasey action for the focused file, the menu will say that no Leasey actions are available.

Listening to Audio Talking Books.

Leasey Media Centre contains special accommodation for listening to audio talking books. These could be files which are numbered sequentially containing audio book narration. They could be books which have a DAISY structure. Leasey Media Centre is not a DAISY player, so it is not possible to navigate by specific leveled headings. But you can play the audio content and navigate through it in a logical manner.

Leasey Media Centre can not work with books which are encrypted in some way, such as books from the National Library Service in the United States. But it is possible to work with books which have a more open framework, such as those from RNIB’s Talking Book service in the United Kingdom.

There are various ways in which you can listen to audio books which will be detailed in this section.

Remember Playback Position.

First, we are going to instruct Leasey Media Centre to remember the last position in the book where we stopped reading.

Step 1. Press Control+Comma for Options.

Step 2. Focus is within the “General” Tab.

Step 3. Press Tab until you reach the Check Box entitled “Resume saved position automatically”.

Step 4. Press Space Bar to check the box.

Step 5. Press Tab to reach the Combo Box entitled “Only Resume Files Longer Than”. This controls how long a file should be for remembering the playback position. To avoid the position within short files such as songs being retained, it is suggested you set the Combo box to 10 minutes.

Step 6. Press Tab repeatedly until you reach OK, then press Enter or Space to save the settings.

Selecting a Book.

There are several methods for selecting an audio book.

Method 1.

Step 1. Move to Audio and Playlists.

Step 2. Press ALT+O to activate the Open folder Button.

Step 3. Choose the folder containing the files you want to play.

Leasey plays the supported audio files in that folder as a temporary list. This does not create a playlist and does not save the folder as a playlist.

Method 2.

Step 1. Using File Explorer within Windows, locate the folder containing the book.

Step 2. Activate the Context Menu.

Step 3. Select the item “Play with Leasey Media Player”.

Step 4. Press Enter.

Leasey plays the supported audio files in that folder as a temporary list. This does not create a playlist and does not save the folder as a playlist.

Method 3.

Step 1. Using Leasey File Manager, locate the folder containing the book.

Step 2. Press Control+Shift+L.

Step 3. Locate the item “Play with Leasey Media Player”.

Step 4. Press Enter.

Leasey plays the supported audio files in that folder as a temporary list. This does not create a playlist and does not save the folder as a playlist.

Listening To a Book and Navigating It.

Having loaded a book, Leasey Media Player should begin playing it from the point where you left off reading.

From this point you can:

  • Play or pause the book. Methods for doing this are described in the Leasey Media Player chapter.
  • Skip forward and back through the book. Methods for doing this are described in the Leasey Media Player chapter.
  • Press Page Up and Page Down to move by book section, such as a chapter.
  • Adjust the speed and volume of playback. Methods for doing this are described in the Leasey Media Player chapter.
  • From the Leasey Media Player window, press Alt+Control+L to open Playback List. This is a simple list of the files currently scheduled to play.
  • In Playback List, use Up Arrow and Down Arrow to choose a book section.
  • Press Enter on a section to start playing it.
  • Press Escape to close Playback List.
  • From the main Media Centre window, press ALT+L to move to the list of files. If you are listening to a DAISY book, where possible Leasey will provide the section names. How useful these are to a large extent depends upon the naming structure from the book producer.
  • Press Enter on a section name to navigate directly to it.
Working with Books Containing Low Audio Level.

Some books can be particularly quiet in terms of audio level. It is possible to adjust the volume of audio to above 100 percent. This needs to be done with some caution so as to avoid playing other files at a high volume.

Step 1. Start playing the book.

Step 2. Press Control+Comma for Options.

Step 3. Press Tab to reach the option entitled “Allow volume above 100 percent”.

Step 4. Press Space Bar to check the box.

Step 5. Press Enter to save.

Step 6. Open up the book as described above and start playing it.

Step 7. Adjust the volume to a level that feels comfortable.

Step 8. Press Control+Shift+V. The volume setting is retained.

Step 9. Lower the volume a little. The reason we are doing this is so that when you come to play other audio content, the volume is not particularly loud.

Step 10. Close the book by pressing ALT+F4.

Step 11. Open up the book again. You should find that the volume has returned to the desired level.

Remembering Speed of Playback.

Under most circumstances, when you adjust speed of playback using the Left and Right Bracket keys, Leasey remembers the speed preference for either podcasts or audio files. However it is possible to remember the speed of playback for a specific item, such as an audio book.

Step 1. Start playing the book.

Step 2. Adjust the speed of playback as required with the Left and Right Bracket keys.

Step 3. Press Control+Shift+Y. This saves the preferred speed of playback for that item.

Clearing Speed and Volume Settings.

You can clear the retention of speed and volume preferences for an item if you wish.

When the item is playing, press ALT+Control+V to clear the volume setting and ALT+Control+Y to clear speed of playback.

Leasey Media Player.

The Leasey Media Player is the player window used by the Media Centre when Leasey Media Player is selected, or when playing local files, playlists and podcasts.

The player can also play the audio soundtrack from supported video files. This includes MP4 and MKV files, and also common formats such as M4V, MOV, AVI, WebM and WMV. Video is not shown; only the audio is played. You can press the Tab key to move through the controls.

The player contains:

  • Play or Pause Button.
  • Stop Button.
  • Mute Button.
  • Record Button, when listening to radio.
  • Stop Recording Button, when listening to radio.
  • Previous track Button, when a playlist is active.
  • Next track Button, when a playlist is active.
  • Back Button.
  • Forward Button.
  • Queue Button.
  • Bookmarks Button.
  • Close Button.
  • Skip amount Combo Box. This determines how much audio is skipped when keystrokes are used, such as Left and Right Arrow, or when the Back and Forward Buttons are activated. Choices include short values such as 5 seconds, 10 seconds or 30 seconds, and longer values such as 10 minutes, 30 minutes or 1 hour.
  • Volume slider.
  • Speed Combo Box.
  • Graphic equaliser preset Combo Box, when playing podcasts, local audio files or local playlists.
  • Graphic bass slider, when the graphic equaliser is available.
  • Graphic treble slider, when the graphic equaliser is available.
Leasey Media Player Keystrokes.
  • Control+Space or letter C plays or pauses.
  • Up Arrow raises the volume by the configured amount, specified in Options.
  • Down Arrow lowers the volume by the configured amount, specified in Options.
  • When focus is on the volume slider, Up Arrow increases by one percent and Down Arrow decreases by one percent.
  • When focus is on the volume slider, Page Up increases by 10 percent and Page Down decreases by 10 percent.
  • Leasey remembers separate volume levels for radio, podcasts, and audio files or playlists.
  • If Allow volume above 100 percent is checked in Options, the player volume can be increased to 200 percent for quiet recordings.
  • Control+Shift+V remembers the current volume for the current item, such as a quiet book, lecture, podcast episode or station.
  • Control+Alt+Shift+V clears the remembered volume for the current item.
  • Control+Shift+Y remembers the current playback speed for the current item, such as a talking book folder, podcast episode or long audio file.
  • Control+Alt+Shift+Y clears the remembered speed for the current item.
  • When focus is on the graphic bass or graphic treble slider, Up Arrow increases by one step and Down Arrow decreases by one step.
  • When focus is on the graphic bass or graphic treble slider, Page Up increases by a larger step and Page Down decreases by a larger step.
  • Alt+M mutes or unmutes.
  • Control+R starts recording the current radio station. If a recording is already running, Control+R stops it. The recording is saved in the folder you chose under Options.
  • Left Arrow skips back by the selected skip amount.
  • Right Arrow skips forward by the selected skip amount.

If Speak player status messages is enabled, Leasey Media Centre speaks the new position after skipping. This is an extremely responsive media player and the ability to skip forward and backward works very well.

  • Page Up moves to the previous track when a playlist is active.
  • Page Down moves to the next track when a playlist is active.
  • Control+Left Arrow moves to the previous chapter when chapter marks exist.
  • Control+Right Arrow moves to the next chapter when chapter marks exist.
  • X moves back to the start of the file.
  • Control+Home also moves back to the start of the file.
  • Numbers 1 through to 9 move to 10 percent through to 90 percent of the file, if the length is known. This also applies to podcast which are streaming.
  • Alt+Shift+T speaks elapsed time.
  • Control+Shift+T speaks remaining time.
  • Control+Alt+T speaks listening time remaining. This takes the current playback speed into account, so it tells you how much real listening time is left rather than the original file time.

ALT+T speaks the total length of the file.

  • Control+I opens a reviewable information window for the current item. It includes details such as the title, podcast name where appropriate, playback position, total duration, time remaining, speed, source type, saved status, bookmark count, bookmark names where available, and whether automatic resume is enabled.
  • Control+J opens Jump to Time.
  • Control+E edits tags for the currently loaded local MP3, M4A, FLAC, OGG or Opus file.
  • Control+Shift+Q opens the Queue Manager.
  • Alt+Control+L opens Playback List for the current sequence of files, such as an audio book folder or selected files played from File Explorer.
  • F4 creates an Audio Note at the current position.
  • F5 lists Audio Notes for the current file.
  • F6 reads the Audio Note at or near the current position.
  • F7 marks the beginning of an audio selection in a local audio file or podcast temporary playback copy.
  • F8 marks the end of an audio selection in a local audio file or podcast temporary playback copy.
  • F9 plays the selected audio without creating a file.
  • F10 creates a new file from the selected audio.
  • Control+F10 appends the selected audio to an existing file of the same format.
  • Left bracket decreases playback speed where speed control is available. This works from the player window.
  • Right bracket increases playback speed where speed control is available. This works from the player window. After changing speed with these keys, Leasey Media Centre speaks the new speed.
  • Left brace decreases the skip amount. This is Shift+Left Bracket on most keyboards.
  • Right brace increases the skip amount. This is Shift+Right Bracket on most keyboards.

The playback queue is temporary. If a track is currently playing, queued files are played after the current track finishes. Queued files play before the next normal playlist track. In the Queue Manager, Enter plays the selected queued item, Delete removes it, and the Buttons allow you to add files, remove files, move them, play the selected item or clear the queue.

One thing you will notice. The number of controls in the audio player differs depending upon the environment. For example, in radio, we do not have the speed control because you cannot vary the speed of playback for a live broadcast. So there is no sense in having it there.

Manual Radio Recording.

When you are listening to radio using the Leasey Media Player, the player contains Record and Stop Recording Buttons. You can also press Control+R to start or stop recording.

Recordings are saved as MP3 or WAV files in the Recording folder specified in Options. You are not asked for a file name each time. Leasey Media Centre creates a file name using the station name and the date and time.

JAWS announces when recording starts. When recording is stopped, JAWS announces that the recording has been saved.

Jump to Time.

To move to a specific time in a file:

Step 1. Press Control+J for Jump to Time.

Step 2. Select the number of hours from the focused List Box with the Up or Down Arrow keys.

Step 3. Press Tab and select the number of minutes from the List Box with the Up or Down Arrow keys.

Step 4. Press Tab and select the number of seconds from the List Box with the Up or Down Arrow keys.

Step 5. Press Enter.

Playback Speed.

The Speed Combo Box changes playback speed. This is especially useful for podcasts and audio books. Radio always plays at normal speed, so the Speed Combo Box is not shown when listening to radio. Podcast speed is remembered separately from local audio files. Local audio files and playlists start at normal speed by default, but if you change the speed for an audio book or similar file, that local audio speed is remembered for future local audio playback. If a particular item needs its own speed, press Control+Shift+Y from the player window. For a folder audio book, this remembers the speed for the whole folder rather than just the current MP3 file. Press Control+Alt+Shift+Y to clear the remembered speed for the current item. Press Control+0 to return to normal speed at any time. Press left bracket to decrease speed or right bracket to increase speed where speed control is available. These keys work from the player window. Press left brace or right brace to decrease or increase the skip amount. These keys work from the player window. These keys have been mentioned here because you may like to increase the speed of audio playback, particularly within speech content such as a podcast, and then use the Left Brack and Right Brace keystrokes to change how far through the audio you move with the Left and Right Arrow keys. It is an excellent combination. So in summary, Left and Right Bracket change speed. Left and Right Brace brackets change skip amount. The Left and Right bracket keys to control the speed of playback are to the immediate right of letter P. Shift with those same keystrokes control the skip amount.

Graphic Equaliser.

The graphic equaliser is available in the Leasey Media Player when playing podcasts, local audio files or local playlists. The graphic equaliser is not shown and is not applied when listening to radio streams. This includes radio streams opened from an M3U or M3U8 file.

The graphic equaliser contains a preset Combo Box, a graphic bass slider and a graphic treble slider. Press Tab to move between the controls.

The graphic equaliser preset Combo Box includes choices such as Off, Speech clarity, Bass boost, Treble boost, Warm, Brighter and Reduce bass. Press Up or Down Arrow keys to change the values. Changing a graphic equaliser preset immediately changes the sound. Changing the graphic bass or graphic treble slider also immediately changes the sound and sets the graphic equaliser preset to Custom.

Chapter Marks.

Some podcast files contain chapter marks. When a local file contains chapter marks, the player title includes the words chapters available. Press JAWS Key+T to read the window title.

Use Control+Left Arrow and Control+Right Arrow to move through the chapters. Press Control+Shift+L to bring into view a list of chapters. Where possible, we obtain the chapter name and start time. Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to find a chapter to listen to, then press Enter.

There are three kinds of chapter marks you may encounter.

Producer Chapters.
  • Some podcasts or audio files already contain chapter marks created by the producer.
  • These are part of the original file.
  • Leasey can use them for navigation, but treats them as read-only.

You can move to a producer chapter by choosing it from the chapter list and pressing Enter. You cannot rename or delete producer chapters from Leasey.

Leasey Chapters.

If you are playing a local MP3 file opened as an audio file, Control+Shift+H opens the Add MP3 Chapter Dialog.

The dialog contains:

  • Chapter title.
  • Time position.
  • Preview.
  • Move earlier.
  • Move later.
  • OK.
  • Cancel.

Type the chapter title in the Chapter title Edit Field.

The Time position Edit Field contains the current playback position. You can edit this value if you need the chapter mark to be more precise.

The time can include tenths of a second. For example:

  • 23.2 means 23.2 seconds.
  • 1:04.5 means 1 minute, 4.5 seconds.
  • 1:04:15.5 means 1 hour, 4 minutes, 15.5 seconds.

Press Enter or Space on Preview to hear a short sample from the proposed chapter point. Preview then returns to the original position and pauses.

Press Enter or Space on Move earlier to move the proposed chapter point back by a quarter of a second.

Press Enter or Space on Move later to move the proposed chapter point forward by a quarter of a second.

When the title and time position are correct, press Enter or Space on OK.

Leasey creates a backup copy of the MP3 before writing chapter metadata. When the chapter has been written, the player refreshes the chapter list so the new chapter can be used immediately.

Chapters created by Leasey are identified in the chapter list as Leasey chapters. The words Leasey chapter are only used in the Leasey chapter list so you know which chapters can be changed. They are not written as part of the chapter title itself.

F2 renames a Leasey chapter. Delete removes a Leasey chapter.

If you rename or delete a Leasey chapter, Leasey rewrites only the chapters it created. Chapter marks created by the podcast or audio producer are preserved.

Suggested Chapters.

If no chapter marks are found for a podcast episode, Leasey can offer to create suggested chapters from the podcast transcript. These are approximate navigation points and are not written to the file unless you specifically choose to make them permanent. If you accept the offer, Leasey prepares topic-based summary chapters and then opens the list when they are ready.

Suggested chapters are most useful for longer podcasts where the provider has not supplied proper chapter marks. They may not be as accurate as chapters created by the podcast producer, but they can still provide a useful way to move through a long episode by topic.

If the current item is a local MP3 file or temporary MP3 playback copy, the suggested chapter list includes a Make Permanent Button. Press Enter or Space on this Button to write the suggested chapters into the MP3 file. Leasey creates a backup copy of the MP3 before writing the chapter metadata. After the chapters have been made permanent, they are shown as Leasey chapters and can be renamed with F2 or removed with Delete.

If the current item is being streamed directly from the internet, suggested chapters can still be used for navigation while the item is loaded, but they cannot be written permanently to the stream.

Because suggested chapters are created from a transcript, they should be regarded as useful guide points rather than exact author-supplied chapters.

Player Information.

Press Control+I from the Leasey Media Player window to open a reviewable information window for the current item.

The information can include:

  • The episode, file or station title.
  • The podcast name, where appropriate.
  • The current playback position.
  • The total duration, where known.
  • The time remaining, where known.
  • The current playback speed.
  • Whether the item is streaming or local.
  • Whether a podcast episode has been saved permanently.
  • The number of bookmarks.
  • Bookmark names, if bookmarks exist.
  • Whether automatic resume playback is enabled.

The information is displayed in an Edit Field so it can be reviewed with normal JAWS reading commands.

Saved Positions.

Saved positions are file specific. This is useful for audio books or long recordings.

When a local file is paused, stopped or closed, the current position is saved. If you open the same file later, you can return to the saved position.

Press Alt+Windows+K globally to resume the saved position, if you have not changed the shortcut in Options. Inside the player, Control+Shift+K also resumes the saved position.

If the file has finished playing, the saved position is reset to the start.

Bookmarks.

Bookmarks are also file specific. They are intended for important points in a long recording or audio book.

To set a bookmark:

Step 1. Move to the position in the document you want to mark.

Step 2. Press Control+K.

Step 3. Type a bookmark name and press Enter.

Moving to a Bookmark.

To move to a bookmark:

Step 1. Press Control+Shift+G.

Step 2. The Bookmarks dialog opens. Move through the bookmarks with Down Arrow. You can also press the first letter of a bookmark name to move quickly through the list.

Step 3. Press Enter to move to the selected bookmark.

Deleting a Bookmark.

To delete a bookmark:

Step 1. Press Control+Shift+G.

Step 2. Press Down Arrow to select the bookmark or type its initial letter.

Step 3. Press Delete.

Audio Notes.

Audio Notes let you attach a written note to a position in a local audio file or podcast temporary playback copy.

They are useful for lectures, training recordings, audio books, interviews or any file where you want to remember what was being discussed at a particular time.

Audio Notes are file specific. They are stored by Leasey Media Centre and do not alter the original audio file.

Creating an Audio Note.

Step 1. Move to the position in the audio where you want the note to be stored.

Step 2. Press F4.

Step 3. Type a name for the note.

Step 4. Press Tab to move to the Note edit field.

Step 5. Type the note text.

Step 6. Press Enter to save the note.

Listing Audio Notes.

To list Audio Notes for the current file, press F5.

Use Up Arrow and Down Arrow to move through the note names.

Press Enter on a note to move to that position in the audio. Leasey Media Player plays a few seconds of audio from that point and then pauses.

Press Delete on a note to delete it.

The Audio Notes dialog also contains an Export Notes Button. This saves the note names, note text and audio positions to a plain text file so the information can be used outside Leasey Media Centre.

Reading an Audio Note.

To read the Audio Note at or near the current playback position, press F6.

The note opens in a read-only edit field. Use the Arrow keys to review the note text.

Press Escape to close the note window.

Announcing Available Audio Notes.

In Options, General, there is a Check Box called Announce when audio notes are available.

When this is checked, JAWS says:

Note, followed by the note name

as playback reaches the position of a saved Audio Note.

Copying and Appending Selected Audio.

Leasey Media Player can copy a useful section of one file to another. It can also append further selected sections to the same file. This works with local audio files and with podcast temporary playback copies.

This is useful if, for example, you want to collect several useful parts of a lecture, interview, podcast or training recording into one new audio file.

To mark and save a section as a new file:

Step 1. Play the local audio file or podcast temporary playback copy.

Step 2. Move to the beginning of the section you want.

Step 3. Press F7.

Step 4. Move to the end of the section you want.

Step 5. Press F8.

Step 6. Press F9 to preview the selected section.

Step 7. Press F10.

Step 8. Choose the file name and location for the new file and press Enter.

The original file is not changed when you use F10. Leasey remembers the file you have just created during the current session, so it is easy to append further selected audio to it. When creating an MP3 segment, Leasey attempts to detect the bitrate of the source file and use that bitrate for the new file. If the bitrate cannot be detected, Leasey uses a safe default.

To append another selected section to a file you have already created:

Step 1. Continue playing the source file, or move to another part of the same file.

Step 2. Mark the next section with F7 and F8.

Step 3. Press Control+F10.

Step 4. Choose the existing file to append to and press Enter.

Only files in the same format as the file currently playing are shown. For example, if you are playing an MP3 file, only MP3 files are shown. Leasey replaces the chosen file after the append has completed successfully. When appending to an existing MP3 file, Leasey attempts to preserve the bitrate of the file being replaced.

You can repeat this process as many times as required:

Step 1. Mark the next useful section.

Step 2. Press Control+F10.

Step 3. Choose the same destination file.

The selected audio is added to the end of that file.

To play the selected section without creating a file:

Step 1. Mark the beginning with F7.

Step 2. Mark the end with F8.

Step 3. Press F9.

Leasey plays the selected section and pauses when the end of the selection is reached.

Determining What Is Playing.

To hear the song title and artist, or file title such as a podcast, press JAWS Key+T, the standard keystroke to read the window title with JAWS.
