The window title has been kept free of content apart from the name of the item which is playing. So it is not going to state the name of the audio player.

Queue Manager.

The Queue Manager is a temporary list of files waiting to be played. It is useful if you are already listening to something and want another file to play next without creating a permanent playlist.

You can open Queue Manager from the player window with Control+Shift+Q. If there are no queued items, Leasey Media Centre reports that no songs are in the queue and does not open an empty dialogbox.

The Queue Manager contains:

  • Queued tracks list.
  • Add file Button.
  • Remove Button.
  • Move up Button.
  • Move down Button.
  • Play Button.
  • Clear Button.
  • Close Button.
Adding a File to the Queue.

Step 1. Open Queue Manager with Control+Shift+Q.

Step 2. Press Enter or Space on Add file.

Step 3. Choose the file using standard Windows techniques and press Enter.

Step 4. The file is added to the queue.

You can also add a file to the queue from File Explorer if File Explorer entries have been registered from Options. Focus the file, press the Applications key or Shift+F10, and choose Add to Leasey Media Centre Queue.

Managing the Queue.

Use Up and Down Arrow in the queued tracks list to move through queued files.

Press Enter on a queued file to play it immediately.

Press Delete or activate Remove to remove the selected file from the queue.

Activate Move up or Move down to change the order. When a queued item is moved, JAWS reports where it has been moved.

Activate Clear to remove all queued items.

The queue is not a permanent playlist. If you want to keep a group of files for later use, create a playlist in the Audio and Playlists area.

Global Player Hotkeys and Shortcut Keys.

To modify any of the shortcut keys for the Media Player, and possibly make some of them global:

Step 1. Press Control+Comma for Options.

Step 2. Press Control+Shift+5 to reach the “Shortcut Keys” tab.

Step 3. Press Tab repeatedly to move through the controls.

The fields are:

  • Actions List.
  • Description Edit Field.
  • Shortcut Key Edit Field.
  • Make This Shortcut Global Check Box.
  • Assign Button.
  • Clear Button.
  • Reset Button.
  • Restore Defaults Button.
  • OK Button.

The Actions list contains all available shortcut actions. When you select an action, Tab to the Description field to hear what the action does, then Tab to the Shortcut key Edit Field if you want to change it.

When focused on an item in the Actions List, JAWS might say: “Show or hide Media Centre, Ctrl+Alt+Win+Z, global”.

This means that the function is Show or Hide Leasey Media Centre, the keystroke is Alt+Control+Windows+Z and the keystroke is global, meaning it can be used from within any application.

If Make this shortcut global is checked, the shortcut works while Leasey Media Centre is running, even if focus is in another application. If Make this shortcut global is unchecked, the shortcut is intended for use only while Leasey Media Centre has focus. Assign stores the shortcut for the selected action. Clear removes the shortcut for the selected action. Reset returns the selected action to its default shortcut. Restore Defaults returns all shortcuts to their default state.

The default global player hotkeys include:

  • Control+Alt+Windows+P plays or pauses.
  • Control+Alt+Windows+S stops.
  • Control+Alt+Windows+Up Arrow raises volume.
  • Control+Alt+Windows+Down Arrow lowers volume.
  • Control+Alt+Windows+M mutes or unmutes.
  • Control+Alt+Windows+Left Arrow skips back.
  • Control+Alt+Windows+Right Arrow skips forward.
  • Control+Alt+Windows+Home moves to the previous track.
  • Control+Alt+Windows+End moves to the next track.

Please note that global shortcut keys may need adjustment if they conflict with other software. If a global shortcut cannot be registered, Media Centre reports the problem without closing.

Examples of hot keys you can type look like this:

  • Play or Pause: Control+Alt+Win+P.
  • Stop: Control+Alt+Win+S.
  • Volume up: Alt+Shift+Up.

It is very difficult to get this wrong. Most similar applications expect you to press the keystroke you want. However this often causes conflicts particularly for JAWS. If you wish to remove a global hot key entirely, remove all the text by pressing Backspace so that the field is empty.

Sound Control.

Sound Control is accessed by pressing the Leasey Key then A for Audio, and selecting the second item, Sound Control. When you press this key combination, the Tasks Combo Box previously referred to is automatically set to the Sound Control area. If you are focused in Leasey Media Centre already, you can press Alt+4.

The Sound Control area provides a simpler way to review and change common Windows sound settings using accessible controls.

The Sound Control area is arranged in two main groups. Output controls come first, followed by recording input controls. This is a very straightforward Dialog Box. Just press the Tab key to move through the controls.

The output controls include:

  • Output devices, headphones or speakers List Box.
  • Set default output Button.
  • Set communications output Button.
  • Application output volumes List Box.
  • Selected application output volume Slider.
  • Mute application output Button.
  • Unmute application output Button.
  • Leasey Media Centre output device Combo Box.
  • Apply Leasey Media Centre output Button.

The output devices list contains the speakers, headphones or other output devices Windows can currently detect. If you want to make the selected device the normal Windows output, activate Set default output. If you want to make it the Windows communications output, activate Set communications output.

Just find the item in the list and then press Tab to move to the appropriate Button. Press Enter or Space to activate it. The Application output volumes list contains running applications which Windows exposes to the volume mixer. Use this list to choose an application, then adjust the Selected application output volume slider or activate Mute application output or Unmute application output.

The Leasey Media Centre output device Combo Box lets you choose the output device used by Leasey Media Centre itself. This duplicates the same option in Options for convenience. Select the named speakers, headphones or audio interface you want to use. The choice is saved until you change it and does not change the Windows output used by other applications.

The recording input controls include:

  • Recording input devices, microphones or line inputs List Box.
  • Set default recording input Button.
  • Set communications recording input Button.
  • Selected recording input level Slider.
  • Mute recording input Button.
  • Unmute recording input Button.

The recording input devices list contains microphones, line inputs or other recording sources Windows can currently detect. If you want to make the selected device the normal Windows recording input, activate Set default recording input. If you want to make it the Windows communications recording input, activate Set communications recording input.

The Selected recording input level slider changes the level for the selected recording input device. Up Arrow increases the level and Down Arrow decreases it.

Loop-back Recording.

Loop-back recording records the audio being played through an output device, such as your speakers, headphones, or audio interface. It is different from recording a microphone or line input.

This can be useful if you want to record a tutorial, a demonstration, a meeting, or other audio which is already being played by the computer. If JAWS is speaking through the same output device, JAWS speech can also be captured. In some situations this is exactly what is wanted, but you should be aware of it.

To make a loop-back recording:

Step 1. In Sound Control, move to the output devices list.

Step 2. Choose the output device whose sound you want to capture.

Step 3. Press Tab to reach the Button Start loop-back recording and press Enter or Space.

Step 4. If necessary, use the Pause loop-back recording Button to pause and resume.

Step 5. Activate the Stop loop-back recording Button when finished.

The recording is saved in the Recording folder specified in Options. The format used is the Recording format specified in Options. For example, if Options is set to MP3 128K, the loop-back recording will be saved in that format.

JAWS Controls.

The JAWS sound controls are at the end of the Sound Control area. These controls manipulate various audio-related functions and include:

  • Route JAWS Sound Left Button.
  • Route JAWS Sound Right Button.
  • Restore Sound Balance Button.
  • Select Next Sound Card Button.
  • Select Previous Sound Card Button.
  • Toggle Audio Ducking Button.

The JAWS Help documentation provides good descriptions of these functions. They are provided here for convenience.

Refreshing the Sound Source List.

Activate Refresh if you have connected or disconnected a sound device and want Leasey Media Centre to rebuild the lists.

Music Recognition.

Music Recognition is accessed using the Leasey Key followed by A. Select the third item which is Music Recognition.

Music Recognition can capture audio from the sound source on your computer which you specify. If for example you hear a song and you would like to identify it for purchasing later, you can capture it.

When recognition is complete, results are produced in a browser because they can include links to sources where the song can be purchased or previewed.

Step 1. From the Combo Box which is focused, press the Down Arrow key to select the sound source containing the music you wish to identify. Many users will not need to be concerned with this.

Step 2. Be sure that music is playing through the sound source specified.

Step 3. Press Tab to reach the Recognise Button and press Enter or Space.

Step 4. Recognition should take between 30 to 45 seconds.

Step 5. If recognition is successful, details are displayed using your default web browser.

Options.

Open Options with Control+Comma.

Options is divided into tabbed pages so related settings are grouped together.

Use Tab and Shift+Tab to move through controls on the current tab. You can also move to each tabbed page using shortcut keys.

The tabs are:

  • General, Control+Shift+1.
  • Radio and Recordings, Control+Shift+2.
  • Podcasts, Control+Shift+3.
  • Windows, Control+Shift+4.
  • Shortcut Keys, Control+Shift+5.
  • Data, Control+Shift+6.
General Tab.
Player.

This group of Radio Buttons lets you choose the player used for radio stations.

The choices are:

  • Winamp.
  • Foobar.
  • VLC.
  • Leasey Media Player.

Leasey Media Player is recommended because it provides the accessible player window, speed control, bookmarks, chapters, queue, sleep timer, recording controls and many of the shortcut keys described in this chapter. The other choices are provided for people who prefer those players for radio listening.

Audio output device.

This Combo Box controls the output device used by Leasey Media Player. Choose the named speakers, headphones or audio interface you want to use. If you have not chosen a device, Leasey selects Windows’ multimedia output, or the first available output if that cannot be resolved. The selected device is saved, rather than following later changes to the Windows default. You can change it here or in Sound Control. Existing choices of a specific output device are preserved. Choose a specific speaker, headset or audio interface if you want Media Centre audio routed there.

Volume step percentage.

This Edit Field controls how much the volume changes when using Media Centre volume commands. For example, typing 1 makes volume adjustments very gradual. Typing 5 changes the volume in five percent steps.

Allow volume above 100 percent.

This Check Box allows Leasey Media Player volume to be raised as high as 200 percent. It is intended for quiet recordings such as some audio books. Use it carefully because a boosted file can be much louder than a radio station or podcast.

Leasey Media Centre remembers separate volume levels for radio, podcasts, and audio files or playlists.

If a particular item is unusually quiet, you can raise the player volume and press Control+Shift+V from the player window. Leasey then remembers that volume only for the current item. For a folder audio book, this remembers the volume for the whole folder rather than just the current MP3 file.

Press Control+Alt+Shift+V to clear the remembered volume for the current item.

Only items for which you explicitly use Control+Shift+V are stored. Leasey does not automatically create a separate volume entry for every file you play. The same principle applies to remembered playback speed, using Control+Shift+Y to remember and Control+Alt+Shift+Y to clear.

Speak player status messages.

This Check Box controls whether Leasey Media Player speaks extra messages during playback. When checked, some actions such as changing volume, changing speed, changing skip amount or moving through a file can be spoken. It is unchecked by default because many people prefer uninterrupted audio.

Announce when audio notes are available.

This Check Box controls whether Leasey Media Player announces Audio Notes during playback.

When checked, Leasey says:

Note, followed by the note name

as playback reaches the position of a saved Audio Note in a local file or podcast temporary playback copy.

It is unchecked by default.

Resume saved position automatically.

This Check Box controls whether Leasey Media Player automatically resumes a local file or downloaded podcast episode from the last saved position.

When checked, pressing Enter on a supported file or podcast episode can begin playback from where you previously stopped, paused or closed it. This is especially useful for podcasts, audio books, lectures and other long recordings.

The manual Resume Saved Position command is still available even if this Check Box is unchecked.

Only resume files longer than.

This Combo Box appears when Resume saved position automatically is checked.

It controls the shortest file length for automatic resume. For example, if this is set to 5 minutes, Media Centre automatically resumes saved positions only for files longer than 5 minutes.

This prevents short songs from unexpectedly starting part way through while still allowing longer podcasts and audio books to resume conveniently.

Radio and Recording Tab.
Recording folder.

This Edit Field specifies where radio recordings and loop-back recordings are saved by default. You can type or paste a folder path. The Browse Button lets you choose the folder using standard Windows techniques.

Recording format.

This Combo Box specifies the recording format.

Choices include:

  • MP3 96K.
  • MP3 128K.
  • MP3 192K.
  • MP3 320K.
  • WAV.

MP3 is usually best if you want smaller files. WAV creates larger files but is uncompressed.

Network caching in milliseconds.

This Edit Field controls buffering for network streams. The normal value is 3000. If a radio stream is unstable or sometimes starts silently, a higher value may help.

Submit stream for sharing.

This Button lets you submit a custom stream to Hartgen Consultancy for review. If approved, it can be added later to the shared Leasey radio directory.

Submit current station.

This Button submits the station you are currently using for review.

Add private stream to favourites.

This Button lets you add a private stream for your own use. It is added to your Favourites and is not submitted for inclusion in the shared directory.

Podcasts Tab.
Import Leasey Recommended Podcasts.

This Button imports the recommended podcast feeds from the Leasey online list.

Import from Previous Leasey Cast Interface.

This Button imports podcast feeds from the older Leasey Cast location. Use this if you previously used the older Leasey Cast interface.

Import OPML.

This Button imports podcast feeds from an OPML file created by another podcast application.

Export OPML.

This Button saves your current podcast feed list as an OPML file. This can be useful for backup or for moving feeds into another podcast application.

Podcast download folder.

This Edit Field specifies where downloaded podcast episodes are saved. You can type or paste a folder path. The Browse Button lets you choose the folder using standard Windows techniques. When an episode is downloaded, Media Centre creates a subfolder named after the podcast feed and saves the episode there.

Download podcast episodes for listening and chapter support.

This Check Box controls whether podcast episodes are downloaded temporarily before playback.

When checked, Media Centre downloads the episode to a temporary listening cache and plays the local copy. This can make chapter marks, bookmarks and saved positions more reliable than streaming directly from the internet.

This setting works particularly well with Options, General, Resume saved position automatically. When both settings are enabled, long podcast episodes can resume from the last saved position when you return to them.

Temporary listening files are not the same as episodes you choose to download and keep.

Clear temporary podcast listening cache.

This Button clears podcast episodes which were downloaded only for listening. It does not remove podcast episodes you deliberately downloaded to keep in your Podcast download folder.

Episode order.

This Combo Box controls how episodes are displayed inside a feed. Choose Newest first if you want the latest episode at the top. Choose Newest last if you prefer to work from oldest to newest.

Remember selected episode in each feed.

This Check Box is unchecked by default. When unchecked, reopening a podcast feed selects its top episode. When checked, Leasey remembers the last selected episode separately for each feed, including after closing and reopening Media Centre. New episodes appearing in the feed do not move your selection to a different episode. This setting remembers your place in the episode list only. It is separate from Resume saved position automatically on the General tab, which controls where audio playback begins within an episode.

Windows Tab.
Minimise to system tray on exit.

When checked, closing Media Centre keeps it running in the Windows system tray. This is important if you want scheduled recordings to occur after you close the main window. When this option is checked, Media Centre also creates the Windows startup shortcut needed to start automatically when Windows starts. You should only use this if JAWS is configured to start automatically after Windows login.

Opening media from File Explorer and other Leasey apps.

When launching files, folders, playlists or audio from another Leasey app, Media Centre opens only the Leasey Media Player window. The full Media Centre window is still available when you launch the app normally.

Register File Explorer entries.

This Button registers Leasey Media Centre with Windows so supported files and folders can be opened, queued, tagged, played or converted from File Explorer. It adds entries such as Play with Leasey Media Centre, Play folder with Leasey Media Player, Add to Leasey Media Centre Queue, Tag with Leasey Tag Editor, and Convert with Leasey Audio Converter where appropriate. If you use Leasey Media Centre as the default player, File Explorer should still show separate file type descriptions such as MP3 audio file, WAV audio file, FLAC audio file or M3U playlist in the Type column. If Windows has already stored older Leasey file associations, running this Button attempts to update those older descriptions automatically. If Windows blocks that update, Leasey Media Centre reports that clearly.

Remove File Explorer entries.

This Button removes Leasey Media Centre entries from File Explorer context menus and removes the Leasey file type registrations. It does not choose a different default player for you. If Leasey Media Centre was the default player for some file types, Windows may ask you to choose another app next time those files are opened.

Cart.

This Button lets you choose one audio file and optionally assign a global shortcut to play it quickly. This is useful for frequently used audio clips.

Shortcut Keys Tab.
Actions list.

This list contains shortcut actions available in the app. Every action is listed even if it currently has no shortcut.

Description.

This read-only Edit Field explains the action selected in the Actions list.

Shortcut key.

This Edit Field lets you type a shortcut such as Control+Alt+P, Shift+F6, Alt+Left, or Control+Alt+Windows+P.

Make this shortcut global.

When checked, the shortcut can work even if focus is outside Media Centre, provided Windows allows it to register. When unchecked, the shortcut works only while Media Centre has focus.

Assign.

This Button stores the shortcut typed for the selected action.

Clear.

This Button removes the shortcut from the selected action.

Reset.

This Button resets only the selected action to its default shortcut.

Restore Defaults.

This Button returns all shortcut assignments to their Media Centre defaults.

Data Tab.

This will be fully described in the chapter of this documentation relating to the Backup and Restore Manager and should generally not be changed here.

Keystroke Summary.

Caps Lock+F1 also opens Context Sensitive Help if you are using the JAWS laptop keyboard layout.

Escape closes most Leasey windows or cancels the current dialog.

Queue Manager.

Playback List.

Leasey Media Player.

Down Arrow decreases volume.

Control+Shift+K resumes the saved position.

F4 creates an Audio Note at the current position.

Control+Shift+L opens the chapter list. If no podcast chapters exist, Leasey can offer to create topic-based suggested chapters from the podcast transcript.

Control+Shift+H opens the Add MP3 Chapter Dialog for writing an embedded chapter mark in a local MP3 file opened as an audio file.

The Add MP3 Chapter Dialog lets you type a title, adjust the precise time position, preview the position, and move the chapter point earlier or later by a quarter of a second.

Control+Comma opens Options from the player.

Sound Control.

Down Arrow decreases a focused volume or level slider.

Enter or Space activates focused Buttons such as Set default output, Mute application output, Start loop-back recording, Pause loop-back recording, Stop loop-back recording, or the JAWS sound controls.

Default Global Player Hotkeys.

Control+Alt+Windows+P plays or pauses.

Leasey Sports and Games

This application contains three methods for obtaining help at any time.

1. Context Sensitive Help.

Context Sensitive Help is available for each control within the application.

When focused upon a control, press Insert+F1 (or Caps Lock+F1) if using the JAWS laptop layout.

An Edit Field is available containing the help information. It will briefly describe the purpose of the focused control together with keystrokes you can use.

Press the Arrow keys to read the help and press Escape to cancel. This will return you back to the control which previously had focus.

2. Leasey Command Centre.

Press Control+Shift+C or Insert+H to open Leasey Command Centre.

The dialog contains:

  • Command Edit Field.
  • Matching commands list.
  • OK and Cancel Buttons.

Press the Tab key to move through the controls.

Focus starts in the Command Edit Field.

Type part of a command name, shortcut, or related word to filter the list.

If the Command Edit Field is empty, pressing Tab moves to the Matching commands list and shows all available commands.

If you have typed text into the Edit Field, the list shows only commands matching the search term.

Use Up and Down Arrow to move through the list.

You will hear the command name, followed by the corresponding shortcut key.

The list therefore serves two purposes. You can press Enter on a command to carry it out, and you can learn the shortcut key for quicker access next time you need to use it.

3. Where Am I?

Press Control+Shift+I for Where Am I. You will receive a succinct summary of where you are located within the focused application.

Introduction.

Perhaps you like to follow your favourite football team, keep an ear on the cricket, or find out who won a game while you were away from your computer. Leasey Sports and Games brings these activities together in one place.

You can look up a score whenever you wish. If you would rather carry on with something else, you can ask Leasey to follow a game for you. This is called monitoring: Leasey checks the game for you. JAWS announces changes as the game progresses. The games you choose to follow make up your monitoring session. You might be writing an email, reading a document or listening to commentary; there is no need to keep returning to the sports window just to find out whether the score has changed.

With Leasey Sports and Games, you can:

  • Find out which games are taking place today, tomorrow or on another date.
  • Look for events involving a particular team or player.
  • Check a live score, or follow up to ten games automatically.
  • Catch up with a team’s most recent result and find its next three games.
  • Read sports headlines, team and player information, and historical articles.
  • Look up available league standings (teams’ positions in a competition) and tennis rankings (players’ positions in a ranking list).
  • Save searches you use regularly and choose how often you hear score updates.

We will work through these activities one at a time. If you are new to Sports and Games, begin by finding a few events and checking a score. Once you are comfortable with that, the monitoring features will be easier to follow.

The team names, scores and fixture times in this chapter are examples to help explain what you may hear. They are not reports of games taking place now. JAWS may describe a control slightly differently according to your speech settings, but the control names will help you find your way.

Opening Leasey Sports and Games.

Step 1. Make sure JAWS is running.

Step 2. Press and release the Leasey Key.

Step 3. Press Shift+G.

Step 4. The Sports and Games window opens. On your first visit, you will be asked to choose your timezone. We will do that in the next section.

Step 5. On later visits, you begin in the Sport list. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose the sport you are interested in.

If Leasey tells you that Sports and Games is already running, bring back its existing window:

Step 1. Press Enter or Space on the message’s OK Button.

Step 2. Press the Hide or restore shortcut. Its initial setting is Control+Alt+G.

See “Choosing your own shortcuts” for how to change this shortcut.

Before you begin: choosing your timezone.

A game may be taking place in another country, but you will usually want to know when it starts where you live. Choosing your timezone allows Leasey to show the dates and times that are useful to you.

For example, if you live in the United Kingdom, choose Europe/London. You do not need to change this when the clocks go forward or back; the seasonal change is taken into account.

Step 1. From the main window, press Control+Comma to open Options. Skip this action if Options is already open. Focus is in Timezone.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to find your timezone. The more commonly used choices are near the beginning of the list. Typing the beginning of a name is another way to find it.

Step 3. Press Tab to Time format.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose 12 hour (AM/PM), such as 3:00 PM, or 24 hour, such as 15:00. You can keep the initial 24 hour choice.

Step 5. Press Tab to News country.

Step 6. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose the country whose sports headlines you would like. This is separate from your timezone.

Step 7. Continue pressing Tab until you reach the OK Button. You will pass some settings for monitoring and shortcuts. You can leave those as they are for now; we will return to them later.

Step 8. Press Enter or Space on the OK Button. Your choices are saved and you return to the main window. You should hear:

Options saved.

You only need to choose your timezone once, although you can return to Options whenever you want to change it. If you press Escape instead of saving, your changes are cancelled. On your first visit, Leasey will ask you to complete the timezone choice before you make a search.

Choosing how times are read.

You may prefer to hear three in the afternoon as 3:00 PM rather than 15:00. Sports and Games lets you choose either style, whichever timezone you use.

Step 1. From the main window, press Control+Comma to open Options.

Step 2. Focus begins in Timezone. Press Tab once to reach Time format. JAWS may say “Time format, 24 hour”.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose 12 hour (AM/PM) or 24 hour. With the 12 hour choice, midnight is 12:00 AM and noon is 12:00 PM.

Step 4. Press Tab until you reach the OK Button.

Step 5. Press Enter or Space. Your choice is saved. Times in results already displayed use the new format, and your selected result is kept.

This choice also applies when you open game details or Announcement history. All of these times follow the timezone selected in Options, including seasonal clock changes. You do not need to hear BST, GMT or another timezone abbreviation after every time.

The initial setting is 24 hour. You can change it whenever you wish. If you press Escape in Options, your previous choice is kept.

Finding your way around the window.

The main window follows the same pattern whichever sport you choose. There is a Sport list, an Action list, any fields needed for your search, a Find Button, and a Results list.

Press Tab to move forward from one control to the next. Press Shift+Tab to move back. When a step says to press Tab until you reach a named control, keep pressing Tab and listening to JAWS until you hear that name.

In a list, use Up or Down Arrow to choose an item. For example, Tab takes you from Sport to Action, while Up or Down Arrow changes the choice within Action. On a Button, press Enter or Space to carry out its action. For a checkbox, press Space to check or uncheck it.

As you Tab through the controls, JAWS announces their Alt-key shortcuts. You can use these same shortcuts whenever you want to reach a field or activate a button. Hold down Alt and press the announced letter; you do not need to press the Leasey Key first. The shortcut belongs to the window you are using. For example, Alt+C checks the selected score in the main window, while Alt+C in Monitored games activates Check now.

The controls appear in this order:

  1. Sport. Choose Soccer, Baseball, Basketball, American football, Tennis, Cricket or Hockey.
  2. Action. Choose what you would like to find, such as Events by date or Live scores.
  3. Date. This is used when you choose Events by date.
  4. Keyword filter, or Keyword: team or player. Here you can enter the name or words you want to search for.
  5. Find. This starts your search.
  6. Results. This contains the events or information returned by your search.
  7. Check score. This asks for the latest score of the selected game.
  8. Monitor game. This follows a live game automatically, or saves a scheduled game to begin checking at its start time.
  9. Open details. This opens the selected information or link.

You will only reach controls that are available for what you are doing. For example, when you choose Live scores, there is no Date field because you are asking about games in progress now. When you choose Sports news, there is no keyword field to fill in.

When you reach an Edit Field, any text already there is highlighted. You can type to replace it, press Backspace to clear it, or press Tab to leave it unchanged. There is no need to press Control+A before entering a different date or team name.

For example, on reaching Date, JAWS may say something like:

Date, edit, today, selected.
  • Typing tomorrow now replaces today. If you want to keep today, press Tab. If you want to change only part of a longer name, use the Left or Right Arrow key to move within the text first.

There is one distinction to keep in mind: Tab moves you to the next field, while Enter in a search field starts the search. So, if you still want to enter a team name after choosing a date, press Tab rather than Enter.

Useful Tip: Alt+S takes you to Sport, Alt+A to Action, Alt+D to Date, Alt+K to the keyword field and Alt+R to Results. Alt+F activates Find. With a game selected, Alt+C checks its score and Alt+M activates Monitor game. Alt+O opens the selected result. You can use these as you become familiar with the window, but it is quite all right to move through it with Tab.

If you used the previous Sports and Games module.

The familiar tasks are still here, but you now choose them within the Sports and Games window. Results appear in its own list. You can use Up or Down Arrow to move through that list, open one result with Enter, then press Escape to close its details and return.

Escape anywhere in the main search window returns you to Sport, just like Alt+S. Your search fields, results and monitoring are kept. Your results remain available. To put the window away while monitoring continues, use the Hide or restore shortcut, initially Control+Alt+G. To close Sports and Games completely, press Alt+F4 in the main window.

The launch command remains Leasey Key followed by Shift+G. The other shortcuts described in this chapter are used directly, without first pressing the Leasey Key.

Listing today’s events.

Before following a game, it helps to know what is being played. Let us begin by looking at today’s soccer events. You can use the same procedure for another sport if you wish.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Soccer.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Events by date.

Step 5. Press Tab to Date. Its contents are highlighted.

Step 6. Type today to replace the highlighted text, or keep today if it is already there. An empty Date field also means today.

Step 7. Press Tab to Keyword filter.

Step 8. Press Backspace to clear any highlighted text. This first search will include all available events for the day.

Step 9. Press Alt+F or Enter to start the search.

Step 10. Wait for the results. Leasey announces how many it has found, and focus moves to the first item in the Results list. If two events were found, for example, you would hear “2 results.”

Step 11. Use Down Arrow to move through the games, or Up Arrow to go back. An entry includes the date, start time, teams or players, and whether the game is scheduled, in progress or finished.

Step 12. Press Enter on a game you want to examine. Its details open in a separate dialogue.

Step 13. Read the details.

Step 14. Press Escape. You return to Results.

To start the search using the Find Button instead of Alt+F, press Tab until you reach Find, then press Enter or Space. Enter in the keyword field is another way to start it.

Here is an example of the sort of entry you might find:

25 May 15:00: Liverpool versus Arsenal. Not Started.

This tells us that the game is due to begin at three o’clock in the afternoon and has not yet started. The time is shown in the timezone you chose earlier. This example uses the 24 hour choice. With 12 hour (AM/PM) selected, the same time is 3:00 PM.

If there are no matches for your search, you will hear:

No matching results found.

You stay in the search controls so that you can change what you entered. There may be no events for that sport on the date you chose.

Useful Tip: You can press Alt+R to return to the Results list whenever you wish. If you switch to another application while a search is being completed, Sports and Games will let you carry on there. Bring its window back when you are ready to read the results.

Finding games involving a particular team.

Some days there are a great many events to read. The Keyword filter is useful when you are interested in just one team, a competition or a country.

Let us imagine that you want to find out whether Liverpool are playing tomorrow.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Soccer.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Events by date.

Step 5. Press Tab to Date.

Step 6. Type tomorrow over the highlighted text.

Step 7. Press Tab to Keyword filter.

Step 8. Type Liverpool.

Step 9. Press Enter to start the search.

Step 10. Read the returned entries with Up or Down Arrow.

Step 11. Press Enter on a game if you would like to read its details.

Step 12. Press Escape when you have finished. You return to the list.

You can use other words in exactly the same way. For soccer, England or Scotland can help find events associated with that country. For baseball, Chicago can find teams with Chicago in their name. Cubs may return more than one team, so listen to the full names before choosing a game.

The filter uses the information available for each event. A broad word may match a country, a competition or a team name. If the result is not quite what you intended, try a more specific name, such as Chicago Cubs instead of Cubs.

Keeping a filter for next time.

Leasey remembers the text used in your last search for each sport. This includes live scores, recent results, upcoming games, information and history, as well as Events by date. Changing the action keeps the text already entered, and your last search text is available again after you close and reopen the app. This saves typing when you usually follow the same team or country.

For example, if you searched for Liverpool last time, JAWS may say something like this when you next reach that field:

Keyword filter, edit, Liverpool, selected.
  • Pressing Tab without typing keeps Liverpool as the filter. Typing England replaces it. Pressing Backspace clears it so that you can see all the events for your chosen date.

Each sport keeps its own filter. Choosing England for soccer will not apply that word to your baseball search. Before assuming that a game is missing, it is always helpful to listen to the contents of the filter field.

If you have moved the cursor within the field to read or edit the text, Control+A will select it all again. You can then replace it or clear it with Backspace.

Choosing another date or the current hour.

You are not limited to today’s events. Perhaps you want to see tomorrow’s fixtures, or catch up with the final scores from yesterday.

In the Date field, you can enter:

  • today, or leave the field empty, for today’s events.
  • tomorrow for the following day.
  • yesterday for the preceding day.
  • hour for games scheduled to start during the current clock hour.
  • Four digits for a date in the current year, with the month first. For example, 0525 means May 25.
  • A full date with the year first. For example, 2027-05-25 means May 25, 2027.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose your sport.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Events by date.

Step 5. Press Tab to Date. Its contents are highlighted.

Step 6. Type the word or date you want. For example, type yesterday.

Step 7. Press Tab to Keyword filter.

Step 8. Choose the filter for this search. Keep the existing text, type a different filter, or press Backspace to clear it.

Step 9. Press Tab until you reach the Find Button.

Step 10. Press Enter or Space to start the search.

Step 11. Use Up or Down Arrow to read the results. Games that have finished include their available final scores.

The word hour is useful if you are wondering what is about to begin. For example, at 3:20 in the afternoon, it looks for games scheduled to start between 3:00 and 3:59 in your chosen timezone. A game that began at two o’clock may still be in progress, but it would not be included in that search. To find games that are already being played, use Live scores, described shortly.

Reading more about a result.

The Results list gives you a useful overview. You do not have to listen to a long description of every game as you move through it. When something interests you, open its details.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+R to reach Results. You can also press Tab until you reach the Results list.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose a game.

Step 3. Press Alt+O or Enter. The Match details dialogue opens, with focus in its Details field.

Step 4. Read the text using your usual JAWS reading commands. As well as the score, you may find the competition, venue, stage of play and the time the score was last checked.

Step 5. If you would like to copy the information, press Tab until you reach Copy all.

Step 6. If you moved to Copy all, press Enter or Space to copy the text. You can now paste it into an email or document.

Step 7. Press Escape to return to your previous control.

To close details using its Button:

Step 1. Press Tab until you reach Close.

Step 2. Press Enter or Space.

Opening details shows the information already obtained for that result. If you want to ask for a newer score, press Escape to close the details, then press Alt+C to check the selected game. After hearing the score, press Enter in Results to open the details again.

Some results, such as news headlines and video links, open in your web browser instead. After reading or watching them, use Alt+Tab to return to Sports and Games.

Reading one piece of information at a time.

Sometimes you may want to hear just the starting time of each game, or compare the points held by several teams. You can do this with virtual columns. If you have used this feature in Leasey Database, the keys will already be familiar.

A virtual column is one piece of information from an entry. For a game, that could be its name, sport, starting time, status or score. For a league table, it could be the team, position, wins or points. You can listen to each piece separately, and the same short message is sent to your Braille display.

You do not have to turn this feature on. Ordinary Up and Down Arrow still let you read the list in the usual way. Use the extra keys whenever you want a closer look at one part of an entry.

Exploring a game in Results.

Step 1. Find some games using a search procedure in this chapter.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow in Results to select a game. Alt+R returns to Results if focus is elsewhere in the main window.

Step 3. Press Alt+Home to reach the first column. For a game, this is Game. You will hear the two teams or players.

Step 4. Press Right Arrow to move to Sport. You hear the column name and its value.

Step 5. Press Right Arrow again to reach Competition. You hear that column name and its value.

Step 6. Continue pressing Right Arrow to review Start, Status, Score, Elapsed time or period clock, Venue and Country. A value is described as unavailable if it has not been supplied.

Step 7. Press Left Arrow to go back one column. Alt+Home returns to the first column; Alt+End goes to the last. At either end, Start of columns or End of columns is followed by the current information.

Step 8. Press Enter if you would like to open the full details for the game you last reviewed.

Step 9. Press Escape when you have finished. You return to the list.

Useful Tip: Use Left Arrow and Right Arrow on their own when moving between columns. Alt+Left Arrow keeps its usual purpose of returning to your last events search.

Comparing the same information across games or teams.

Let us imagine that you are in a hockey standings window and want to compare team points.

Step 1. Press Tab until you reach Teams.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to select a team.

Step 3. Press Alt+Home to reach Team.

Step 4. Press Right Arrow three times, passing Group and Position, to reach Points.

Step 5. You might hear something like this:

Points: 12.

The figure depends on the table you are reading. To check which team you have reached, press Alt+Home to hear its name, then press Right Arrow three times to return to Points.

Step 6. Press Alt+Down Arrow to hear the points for the next team. You hear the figure, such as 9, without the column heading. Alt+Up Arrow moves to the previous team.

Step 7. Continue with Alt+Down Arrow to compare more teams. Alt+Up Arrow takes you back through the same column. At the ends of the list, you hear Start of items or End of items. The list does not wrap round to the other end.

Step 8. Press Left Arrow or Right Arrow if you want another field for the team you have reached. You might compare wins next, for example.

Step 9. Press Enter to open details for the team you last reviewed.

Step 10. Press Escape to return to that team.

Step 11. Press Escape again when you want to close the standings window.

You can use the same method in Results. For example, reach Start with Right Arrow, then use Alt+Down Arrow to compare starting times. In tennis rankings, you could review Ranking points in the same way.

Knowing which item an action will use.

While you browse with Alt+Up Arrow or Alt+Down Arrow, the visible selection stays in place. This avoids JAWS repeatedly reading the whole row while you are trying to hear one field. Focus also remains in the list.

The item you last reviewed is the one used when you press Enter or perform an action for a single item. In Results, this includes Check score, Monitor game and Open details. In Monitored games, Details, Remove and Delete use the game last reviewed. The removal confirmation names both teams. Check those names before approving removal.

The Check now Button in Monitored games continues to check the saved session. Pause and Reinstate also apply to the session as a whole.

To resume ordinary list navigation, press Up or Down Arrow without Alt. Navigation continues from the item you last reviewed. Home and End return to their usual job of reaching the first and last entries.

Where Am I also identifies the item and column you are reviewing. Press Control+Shift+I whenever you want that reminder.

If monitoring changes the order of the games, your column review follows the same game. If that game finishes and disappears, trying to open or remove it tells you that it is no longer in the list. Choose another item with an arrow key before carrying out an action. A different game will not be removed in its place.

Using columns in the other lists.

Virtual columns are available in Results, Monitored games, all standings and rankings lists, team and player choices, article choices, saved favourites and the Matching commands list in Leasey Command Centre.

In Monitored games, the extra Monitoring column tells you whether the game is waiting or being followed, and whether monitoring is paused. Last check identifies a reported checking error when there is one.

In Favourites, the columns are Sport, Action and Keyword. In Command Centre, they are Command and Shortcut. After reviewing an item, press Enter in the list or Tab to the OK Button and press Enter or Space to use that item.

Some short choice lists contain only a name, so there is just one column. Alt+Up Arrow and Alt+Down Arrow can still browse those entries. The Sport, Action and Options drop-down controls keep their usual arrow-key behaviour.

Changing a standings filter or running a new search starts review from the newly selected entry. Column browsing uses the information already in the list. It does not make another request for a score or table, and it does not add these field messages to Announcement history.

For a reminder while you are in a list, press Insert+F1. Read Leasey Help with the arrow keys and press Escape to return. You can also open Leasey Command Centre from the list and type column to find its column-browsing commands.

A note about cricket events.

Cricket needs a little extra explanation because a game can continue for several days. You would not want to miss an ongoing game simply because its first day of play was yesterday.

When you ask for today’s cricket events, Leasey also includes ongoing games that began on an earlier day. These appear before the other fixtures in the list.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Cricket.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Events by date.

Step 5. Press Tab to Date.

Step 6. Type today.

Step 7. Press Tab to Keyword filter.

Step 8. Type England to find games involving England. To include all available games instead, press Backspace to clear the selected text.

Step 9. Press Alt+F to search.

Step 10. Wait for focus to move to Results.

Step 11. Use Up or Down Arrow to read the games. Listen to the teams and stage of play. An ongoing cricket game may show an earlier starting date.

Step 12. With the required game selected, press Tab until you reach Check score.

Step 13. Press Enter or Space to ask for the latest score.

Step 14. Press Alt+R to return to Results.

Step 15. Press Enter if you would like to read the additional innings information.

For example, part of the information you hear might be:

England 120 for 3 after 16 overs and 2 balls.

This gives the runs, wickets and overs for that innings. A lunch break, tea interval or other pause in play does not necessarily mean the game has finished. If you choose to monitor it, Leasey continues following it until it receives an ending result or you stop monitoring yourself.

Checking the current score.

There are two ways to keep up with a game. You can check its score once, whenever you feel like it, or ask Leasey to monitor it and tell you about changes automatically.

We will begin with a single score check. This does not start monitoring, so it is a useful choice if you only want a quick update.

Looking up a live game by name.

Imagine that a Liverpool game has begun and you would like to know the score.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Soccer.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Live scores.

Step 5. Press Tab to Keyword: team or player.

Step 6. Type Liverpool.

Step 7. Press Enter while you are still in the keyword field to start the search.

Step 8. When the results arrive, listen to the teams.

Step 9. If more than one game matches, use Up or Down Arrow to select the one you mean.

Step 10. Press Enter to open its details. You might hear information such as:

Liverpool versus Arsenal. Liverpool 1, Arsenal 0. First Half.

Step 11. Read any additional information you want.

Step 12. Press Escape to return to Results.

Step 13. When you want another update, press Tab until you reach Check score.

Step 14. Press Enter or Space. The new score is announced.

Step 15. Press Alt+R to return to Results. Alt+C checks the score without leaving the list as an alternative to the Button.

Instead of Enter in the keyword field, you can reach Find with Tab and press Enter or Space to search.

In this example, Liverpool are leading by one goal and the game is in its first half. Other sports use their own terms. For baseball you may hear the innings, while a tennis result can include sets, points and the player who is serving.

For tennis, choose Tennis in Sport and enter a player’s name in the keyword field. For cricket, choose Cricket and enter England. To find all the available live games for your chosen sport, press Backspace in the keyword field to clear its highlighted text, then press Enter to search.

Useful Tip: With a game selected in Results, press Alt+C to check its score without moving away from the list.

A game that has only just begun may take a little time to appear as live. Give the service a minute or so to catch up, then try again if necessary.

Checking a game you found in an events list.

You may already have today’s events in front of you. There is no need to type a team name again just to check one of them.

Step 1. Press Alt+R to reach Results.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to select the game you want.

Step 3. Press Tab until you reach Check score.

Step 4. Press Enter or Space.

Step 5. Wait for JAWS to announce the returned score.

Step 6. Press Alt+R to return to Results. The game’s entry now contains the information just received.

If you prefer to stay in the list, use Alt+C instead of reaching and activating Check score. This is especially convenient when several interesting games are taking place at once.

Checking several scores in turn.

Step 1. Follow the steps under Listing today’s events. When the results arrive, focus moves to Results. If you have moved elsewhere in the main window, press Alt+R to return to the list.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to select the first game you want to check.

Step 3. Press Alt+C. Your place in the list is kept.

Step 4. Listen to the score.

Step 5. Press Down Arrow to move to another game of interest.

Step 6. Press Alt+C again. Repeat the move-and-check actions for any other games you want to check.

You can leave these results available and return to them later with Alt+R. Checking several scores in this way still does not start automatic monitoring.

Monitoring a game for score changes.

Suppose you are interested in a game but also have some work to do. Rather than checking the score yourself every few minutes, you can ask Leasey to keep checking it for you. This is called monitoring.

Once you have added a game, you can move to another application. When Leasey finds a change in the score or the stage of play, JAWS announces it. The announcement includes the teams or players, so you know which game it belongs to.

To begin with, Leasey checks every 30 seconds. You can choose a longer interval if you prefer. We will explain that after working through the basic monitoring controls.

If this is your first time using monitoring, try one game to become familiar with what you hear. You can add others whenever you wish.

Starting from a live-score search.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose your sport. For this example, choose Soccer.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Live scores.

Step 5. Press Tab to the keyword field.

Step 6. Type the team name over any highlighted text. For example, type Liverpool.

Step 7. Press Enter in the keyword field to start the search. Alt+F is an alternative.

Step 8. Wait for focus to move to Results.

Step 9. Use Up or Down Arrow to select the game you want to follow.

Step 10. Press Alt+M to activate Monitor game.

Step 11. Listen for the confirmation. If the selected game is Liverpool against Arsenal and your interval is 30 seconds, the message will be:

Monitoring added for Liverpool versus Arsenal. Interval 30 seconds.

Step 12. You can now use Alt+Tab to work in another application. If you want to hide the Sports and Games window, use its Hide or restore shortcut, initially Control+Alt+G.

To use the Monitor game Button instead of Alt+M:

Step 1. Press Tab until you reach Monitor game.

Step 2. Press Enter or Space.

Leasey will carry on checking while the window is hidden. Leave the application running: Alt+F4 closes it completely and stops its checks.

Starting from an events list.

You can also start monitoring a game you have found among today’s events.

Step 1. Follow “Listing today’s events”, choosing the sport you want. In the keyword field, you can type a team name if you want to narrow the results.

Step 2. When focus moves to Results, use Up or Down Arrow to select the game you want.

Step 3. Check the entry for its start time and status.

Step 4. If you want the latest information before proceeding, press Alt+C.

Step 5. Listen to any requested update before continuing.

Step 6. If the game is in progress or has a confirmed scheduled start time, press Tab until you reach Monitor game.

Step 7. If you reached Monitor game, press Enter or Space. Alt+M is an alternative while the game is selected in Results.

Step 8. Listen for the confirmation that monitoring has been added.

Step 9. Continue using Sports and Games, switch to another application, or hide the window with Control+Alt+G if you have kept that shortcut.

You can add a game before play begins. Leasey saves the fixture and waits until its listed start time before checking it. If Monitor game is unavailable, the game may have finished, been cancelled or postponed, or be waiting for a confirmed start time. With that game still selected in Results, you can press Alt+C later to ask for its latest details.

Useful Tip: Once you are familiar with the procedure, Alt+C checks the selected score and Alt+M adds the selected live or scheduled game to monitoring. These shortcuts let you keep your place in Results.

Setting up monitoring before a game starts.

Perhaps you have found a baseball game which starts at 10 AM today, but you will be busy by then. You can add it now and let Leasey wait for the start time. There is no need to return at ten o’clock to press another button.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Baseball.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Events by date.

Step 5. Press Tab to Date.

Step 6. Type today.

Step 7. Press Tab to the keyword field.

Step 8. Type a team name. To see all games instead, press Backspace to clear the highlighted text.

Step 9. Press Tab until you reach Find.

Step 10. Press Enter or Space.

Step 11. Wait for focus to move to Results.

Step 12. Use Up or Down Arrow to select the game starting at 10 AM. Times use the timezone and format chosen in Options.

Step 13. Press Tab until you reach Monitor game.

Step 14. Press Enter or Space. Alt+M is an alternative while the game is selected in Results.

Step 15. Listen for the confirmation. For a Toronto versus New York fixture, for example, JAWS will say that monitoring is scheduled, give the date and time when checks will begin, and remind you to keep the application open.

Check the scheduled game.

Continue here after Leasey confirms that monitoring is scheduled.

Step 1. Press Control+M. Monitored games opens with focus in its list.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to find the fixture. It is marked Waiting until, followed by the date and start time. Games already in progress continue to be checked.

Step 3. Press Escape to close Monitored games.

Step 4. Use Alt+Tab to return to your work. Keep Sports and Games open and the computer awake. You can hide the app with its Hide or restore shortcut.

At the listed start time, Leasey begins checking that particular fixture. If play has not begun, the entry changes to Waiting for play to begin. Leasey keeps checking at your chosen interval and announces when the sports service reports play or a score change. A delayed start does not require you to add the game again.

Leasey makes no automatic score requests for that game before its saved start time. Check now and Show scores also leave future games waiting. If every game in your session is scheduled for later, you will hear “Scheduled games are waiting for their start times.”

If a check returns a changed start time, Leasey tells you and waits for the new time if it is still in the future. If the sports service temporarily cannot find the fixture, Leasey keeps it saved and retries, leaving longer between failed checks. A confirmed cancellation or final result removes the game from monitoring.

To cancel a planned start, use “Stopping just one game”. Select the scheduled fixture in Monitored games, request removal with Delete or the Remove Button, and check the named game before confirming. Escape returns to the main window.

Pause stops automatic checks for the whole session, including planned starts. Reinstate resumes the session; future games still wait for their own time. The sections Stopping monitoring for a while and Resuming a paused session explain these controls step by step. If you close the app while monitoring is running, reopening it resumes the saved session automatically. A session you deliberately paused stays paused.

The same procedure works for the other supported sports when a fixture has a confirmed start time. You can save up to ten live and scheduled games in total.

What you will hear.

If the score changes in our example game, an announcement might be:

Liverpool versus Arsenal. Liverpool 2, Arsenal 0. Second Half.

You may also hear that a game has reached half-time, that another innings has begun, or that play has finished. The terms depend on the sport and the information available.

You will not hear the same score repeated every 30 seconds simply because another check has taken place. Leasey announces a change in the score or match status. If you turn on Announce clock changes while monitoring in Options, you also hear changes to the game clock when the sports service provides one.

This means that a quiet period can be quite normal. If you would like reassurance that checks are taking place, you can enable the optional click sound described later. You can also ask for a fresh score whenever you want.

When the sports service reports that a game has finished or been cancelled, Leasey removes it from monitoring. You may hear, for example:

Monitoring finished for Liverpool versus Arsenal.

Other games you are following continue as before. When the last game has finished, there is nothing further for Leasey to monitor.

Hearing changes to the game clock.

Perhaps you would like to know that play is progressing even when the score has not changed. A checkbox in Options lets you hear changes to the game clock for all sports that supply one.

Step 1. From the main window, press Control+Comma to open Options.

Step 2. Press Tab until you reach Announce clock changes while monitoring. This checkbox is initially unchecked.

Step 3. Check its current state.

Step 4. Press Space if you need to check it.

Step 5. Press Tab until you reach OK.

Step 6. Press Enter or Space to save and return to the main window.

Step 7. Monitor a game in the usual way. At each normal check, Leasey announces a new clock reading if one is available. It names the game and the stage of play, so you can tell which game you are hearing. The message also appears in Braille and Announcement history.

For a Premier League soccer game, part of the announcement might be:

Clock: 73 minutes out of 90 minutes of normal time.

Added time is described separately when it is supplied. For example, you might hear 90 minutes out of 90 minutes of normal time, plus 4 minutes of added time. The match is not removed just because the clock reaches 90 minutes; Leasey waits for the sports service to report that it has finished.

A quarter or period clock belongs to that part of the game. It is not presented as the elapsed time for the whole match. Known normal playing time is included for the NFL, NBA, WNBA and NHL, and for recognised senior soccer competitions. For other competitions, Leasey reads the supplied clock without guessing a total. Extra time and overtime may make a game longer than normal playing time.

Some games do not supply a clock. Baseball, cricket and tennis do not have a fixed total playing time in minutes; their innings, overs, sets and scores remain available as usual. This option cannot make missing information appear, and it does not estimate a clock from the time on your computer.

The same clock reading is not repeated at every check. If both the score and clock change, they are combined in one update. To stop clock announcements, repeat the steps above and press Space to uncheck the checkbox before saving Options.

Following more than one game.

There may be several games you would like to keep up with on a busy afternoon. You can follow up to ten at once, and they can be from different sports. For example, you could follow a soccer match and a cricket game together.

Step 1. Add your first game using either of the procedures above.

Step 2. Press Alt+R to return to Results.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow to select another live or scheduled game. For a different sport or team, run a search with the new choices first.

Step 4. If you need to update the game’s status, press Alt+C.

Step 5. Listen to the requested update.

Step 6. Press Alt+M to add the selected game to monitoring.

Step 7. Listen for the confirmation that this game has also been added.

Step 8. Repeat for any other live or scheduled games you would like to follow, up to a total of ten.

Step 9. Press Control+M to open Monitored games.

Step 10. Use Up or Down Arrow to review the full list of games.

Step 11. Press Escape to return to the main window.

Searching for another team does not remove the games you have already added. You can explore other results while monitoring continues.

Live games use the same checking interval. Each scheduled game waits for its own start time; it does not delay checks on games already in play. When one game’s score changes, you hear about that game; Leasey does not read out every unchanged score as well.

A game can only be added once. If you try to add it again, Leasey explains that it is already in your monitoring session. A session is the list of games you have chosen to follow.

There is one point to remember if you have paused an earlier session. Adding a new game starts monitoring for the whole saved list, including those earlier games. If you only want to follow the new game, remove the unwanted games first. The next sections explain how.

Reviewing the games you are following.

The Monitored games dialogue brings together the controls for reviewing, checking, pausing and removing games. This is a useful place to visit whenever you want to manage what Leasey is following.

Step 1. Use Alt+Tab to bring the Sports and Games window forward. If it is hidden in the system tray, use your Hide or restore shortcut, initially Control+Alt+G.

Step 2. From the main window, press Control+M. This opens Monitored games, with focus in the list.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow to read the games and their last known scores. Games saved in advance are marked Waiting, with their scheduled start time.

Step 4. Press Enter to read more about the selected game. Its details open.

Step 5. Press Escape when you have finished reading them.

Step 6. Press Alt+C to activate Check now.

Step 7. Wait for Leasey to receive the scores. Games scheduled for later keep waiting until their start time.

Step 8. If focus is on Check now, press Shift+Tab to return to the games list.

Step 9. Use Up or Down Arrow to review the games again.

Step 10. When you have finished, press Tab until you reach Close.

Step 11. Press Enter or Space. You return to the main window.

To use the Check now Button instead of Alt+C:

Step 1. Press Tab until you reach Check now.

Step 2. Press Enter or Space.

After the games list, the buttons are Check now, Details, Remove, Pause, Reinstate and Close. We will use Pause, Reinstate and Remove in the following sections.

Opening Monitored games shows the latest scores already held by Leasey. Check now asks for fresh information. If nothing has changed, you may hear:

Score check complete. Scores unchanged.
  • Closing this dialogue does not stop monitoring. It returns you to the main window.
Asking for scores while you are in another application.

Perhaps you have set the checking interval to five minutes, but the game is getting exciting and you do not want to wait. The Show scores shortcut gives you an update whenever you want one.

Step 1. While Sports and Games is running, press the Show scores shortcut. Its initial setting is Control+Shift+S.

Step 2. Sports and Games comes forward and opens Monitored games. It also asks for a fresh check of your saved games.

Step 3. Wait for the scores to arrive. Previous scores may appear first while the check is taking place.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to read the list.

Step 5. Press Enter on a game if you want more detail.

Step 6. Press Escape when you have finished reading its details.

Step 7. Press Tab until you reach Close.

Step 8. Press Enter or Space. You return to the main Sports and Games window.

Step 9. Use Alt+Tab to return to your work, or use Hide or restore to hide Sports and Games.

Show scores checks the games in your saved session whose start time has arrived. Games scheduled for later are still listed, but are not checked early. By comparison, Alt+C in the main Results list checks just the selected game.

Stopping monitoring for a while.

You may need to take a phone call, concentrate on a document or simply have a break from score announcements. Pause lets you stop the automatic checks without having to find all your games again later.

Step 1. Use Alt+Tab to return to Sports and Games. If you hid it, use your Hide or restore shortcut, initially Control+Alt+G.

Step 2. If a dialogue is open, press Escape until you return to the main window. Escape in Options cancels unsaved changes.

Step 3. Press Control+M to open Monitored games.

Step 4. Press Tab until you reach the Pause Button.

Step 5. Press Enter or Space. JAWS announces:

Monitoring stopped. The session is saved for reinstatement.

Step 6. Press Tab until you reach the Close Button.

Step 7. Press Enter or Space. Your games remain saved, but Leasey has stopped checking them automatically.

Pause applies to all the games in your session, rather than only the one highlighted in the list. If you just want to stop following one game, use Remove as described below.

Useful Tip: In Monitored games, Alt+P activates Pause. Control+P performs the same action from the main window. On the Monitoring menu it is called Stop monitoring, keep session.

An announcement that JAWS had already begun or had waiting to speak may still be heard. You can also deliberately ask for a single update while paused: Check now and the Show scores shortcut both work without restarting automatic monitoring.

Resuming a paused session.

When you are ready to hear score changes again, use Reinstate. This resumes the games you kept in your saved list.

Step 1. Use Alt+Tab to return to Sports and Games. If you hid it, use your Hide or restore shortcut, initially Control+Alt+G.

Step 2. If a dialogue is open, press Escape until you return to the main window.

Step 3. Press Control+M to open Monitored games.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to review the saved games.

Step 5. Remove any unwanted game using “Stopping just one game” before continuing.

Step 6. Press Tab until you reach Reinstate.

Step 7. Press Enter or Space.

Step 8. Listen for the confirmation:

Sports session reinstated.

Step 9. Press Tab until you reach the Close Button.

Step 10. Press Enter or Space. You can now return to your other applications while Leasey follows the games again.

Control+R in the main window is a quicker way to reinstate the session. If the saved list is empty, Leasey explains that you need to add a live or scheduled game first.

Stopping just one game.

Let us imagine that you are following both soccer and cricket, but now only want cricket updates. There is no need to stop everything. Remove the soccer match from your saved list and leave the cricket game there.

Step 1. From the main window, press Control+M to open Monitored games.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to select the game you no longer want to follow.

Step 3. Press Delete. A confirmation names both teams.

Step 4. Read the confirmation to check that it names the game you want to remove.

Step 5. Confirm the removal only if the game is correct.

Step 6. You will hear:

Game removed from monitoring.

Step 7. The game disappears from the list.

Step 8. Use Up or Down Arrow to review the remaining games, if wanted.

Step 9. Press Tab until you reach Close.

Step 10. Press Enter or Space.

With the unwanted game selected in Monitored games, you can use the Remove Button instead of Delete:

Step 1. Press Tab until you reach Remove.

Step 2. Press Enter or Space.

Step 3. Read the game named in the confirmation.

Step 4. Confirm removal only if the named game is correct.

Step 5. Press Shift+Tab until you reach the games list.

Step 6. Use Up or Down Arrow to review the remaining games, if wanted.

Step 7. Press Tab until you reach Close.

Step 8. Press Enter or Space to return to the main window.

The other games continue if monitoring was running. If you had paused the session, they remain paused.

Reinstate resumes the games still in the list; it does not bring back a game you removed. If you change your mind, repeat the earlier search steps to find that game again. Select it in Results with Up or Down Arrow and press Alt+M to add it while it is still live or scheduled with a confirmed start time.

Starting with a fresh list.

Pause keeps your games, whereas Remove takes them out of the list. If you want a completely fresh session, you can clear the unwanted games one at a time.

Step 1. From the main window, press Control+P to pause monitoring.

Step 2. Press Control+M to open Monitored games.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow to select an unwanted game.

Step 4. Press Delete. The removal confirmation appears.

Step 5. Read the game named in the confirmation.

Step 6. Confirm removal if it is the game you intend to remove.

Step 7. Repeat the selection and confirmation procedure until the list is empty, or contains only games you want to keep.

Step 8. Press Tab until you reach the Close Button.

Step 9. Press Enter or Space.

Step 10. Use a search procedure in this chapter to find the new live or scheduled games you want.

Step 11. Use Up or Down Arrow in Results to select a game.

Step 12. Press Alt+M to add it. Repeat for any other games you want to follow.

The ten-game limit includes games scheduled for later and games kept in a paused session. Removing old games makes room for new ones. Remember that adding a new game starts monitoring for the whole remaining list.

Returning after Sports and Games has been closed.

Your list of games is saved when you close Sports and Games. If monitoring was running, it resumes automatically when you open the app again. Games scheduled for later wait for their start times. Games already due or in progress are checked. There is no need to remember to press Reinstate each time you open the app.

Step 1. Open Sports and Games with the Leasey Key followed by Shift+G.

Step 2. Press Control+M to review the saved games.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow to review the saved games.

Step 4. Remove any unwanted games using “Stopping just one game”, including its confirmation step.

Step 5. If you deliberately paused monitoring before closing the app and want to resume it, press Tab until you reach Reinstate. Otherwise, the previously active session is already running.

Step 6. Press Enter or Space on Reinstate if you chose to resume the paused session.

Step 7. Press Escape to close Monitored games when you are ready to continue with your work.

If a game finished while the application was closed, Leasey removes it when the next successful check confirms that it has ended.

If you need to restart JAWS.

You do not lose the saved list just because you need to restart JAWS. If Sports and Games has remained open, you can return to it afterwards and review the scores.

Step 1. Restart JAWS in the usual way.

Step 2. Use Alt+Tab to return to Sports and Games. If you hid it, use your Hide or restore shortcut, initially Control+Alt+G.

Step 3. From the main window, press Control+M to open Monitored games.

Step 4. Press Alt+C to check the current scores.

Step 5. If you had paused monitoring and want it to continue, press Tab until you reach Reinstate.

Step 6. If you chose to resume the paused session, press Enter or Space on Reinstate.

Step 7. Press Escape to return to the main window.

Step 8. If Sports and Games was also closed, use the reopening procedure above.

Choosing how often Leasey checks.

The best checking interval depends on how you like to follow a game. You may want frequent updates during a close tennis match, but prefer fewer interruptions while working. You can change the interval even after monitoring has started.

Step 1. From the main window, press Control+Comma to open Options.

Step 2. Press Tab until you reach Check interval.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose 30 seconds, 1 minute, 2 minutes, 3 minutes, 4 minutes or 5 minutes.

Step 4. Press Tab until you reach the OK Button.

Step 5. Press Enter or Space to save your choice.

The initial setting is 30 seconds. If you change it to five minutes, Leasey checks less often; if you later change it back to 30 seconds, it checks more often again.

A shorter interval cannot make the sports service report a score before it has received it. Allow for a little delay between something happening in the game and hearing about it. If you want an update before the next automatic check, press Control+M in the main window, then Alt+C in Monitored games. Press Escape to return. You can also use your Show scores shortcut, initially Control+Shift+S, from another application.

Hearing a click when a check begins.

This option plays the Leasey sports monitoring sound. It can be reassuring when a game has been quiet for a while. It lets you know that Leasey is checking, even when there is no new score to announce. On the other hand, you may prefer silence if you are listening to commentary.

Step 1. Open Options from the main window with Control+Comma.

Step 2. Press Tab until you reach Play a click when checking scores.

Step 3. Check whether the box is checked or unchecked.

Step 4. Press Space if you need to change it. Checked enables the sound; unchecked disables it. JAWS tells you the new state.

Step 5. Press Tab until you reach the OK Button.

Step 6. Press Enter or Space.

The click is off to begin with. It marks the start of a check; it does not mean that a new score has been found or that the check has already finished.

Choosing whether score announcements interrupt JAWS.

If JAWS is reading a document when a score changes, you may prefer to finish listening before hearing the update. At other times, the score may be the information you want immediately. The interruption setting lets you choose.

Step 1. From the main window, press Control+Comma to open Options.

Step 2. Press Tab until you reach Interrupt JAWS speech for score announcements.

Step 3. Check whether the box is checked or unchecked.

Step 4. Press Space if you need to change it. Checked allows score announcements to interrupt JAWS; unchecked keeps the current speech from being interrupted.

Step 5. Press Tab until you reach the OK Button.

Step 6. Press Enter or Space to save your choice.

Interruption is off to begin with. You can return to this setting whenever your preference changes. As with the other Options settings, pressing Escape cancels any changes you have not saved.

Catching up with an announcement you missed.

You may be distracted just as JAWS reads an important score. Announcement history lets you go back over recent score messages and confirmations.

Step 1. Use Alt+Tab to return to Sports and Games. If you hid it, use your Hide or restore shortcut, initially Control+Alt+G.

Step 2. If a dialogue is open, press Escape until you return to the main window.

Step 3. Press Control+H to open Announcement history.

Step 4. Read the Details field with your usual JAWS reading commands. The newest saved message comes first, followed by earlier messages. Each has a time to help you place it.

Step 5. If you want a copy, press Tab until you reach Copy all.
