Step 6. If you moved to Copy all, press Enter or Space to copy the text.

Step 7. Press Escape to return to the main window.

To close Announcement history using its Button:

Step 1. Press Tab until you reach Close.

Step 2. Press Enter or Space.

Leasey keeps up to 200 messages. Pausing monitoring or removing a game does not erase its earlier announcements. Unchanged scores are not added at every checking interval, so this is a history of announcements rather than a record of every check.

History times and fixture times follow your chosen Timezone and Time format in Options. Changing either setting does not change the stored announcements.

Finding a team’s or player’s most recent result.

With so many events taking place, it is easy to miss a result. Perhaps the New York Mets played while you were away, and you would like to know how they got on. Most recent result is the option to use.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Baseball. For another team or player, choose the appropriate sport.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Most recent result.

Step 5. Press Tab to Keyword: team or player.

Step 6. Type New York Mets. Use at least three characters for a name. For tennis, enter a player’s name.

Step 7. Press Enter in the keyword field to search.

Step 8. If Choose team or player appears, use Up or Down Arrow to select the team you mean. If there is only one match, you go straight to the result.

Step 9. If Choose team or player is open, press Enter to accept your choice. This extra choice distinguishes teams with similar names.

Step 10. When the result arrives, press Enter on it to read the details.

Step 11. Press Escape to close the details and return to Results.

To start the search with its Button instead of Enter in the keyword field, press Tab until you reach Find, then press Enter or Space.

For example, a completed result might be described like this:

New York Mets versus Arizona Diamondbacks. New York Mets 1, Arizona Diamondbacks 5. Finished.

Finished, Final or similar wording tells you that play has ended. Most recent result looks for a completed game. If you want the score of a game still taking place, follow the earlier steps under Looking up a live game by name.

Finding a team’s or player’s next three games.

You might want to plan your listening for the coming week, or find out who your favourite team will be playing next. Next three games gives you the upcoming fixtures that are available.

Let us use Liverpool again for this example.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Soccer.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Next three games.

Step 5. Press Tab to the keyword field.

Step 6. Type Liverpool.

Step 7. Press Enter to search.

Step 8. If a team choice appears, use Up or Down Arrow to select Liverpool.

Step 9. If the team-choice dialogue is open, press Enter to accept your choice.

Step 10. Read the fixtures in Results with Up or Down Arrow. Each entry gives the date, time and teams.

Step 11. Press Enter on a fixture to read its further details.

Step 12. Press Escape to return to the list.

A fixture entry might look like this:

25 May 16:00: Liverpool versus Crystal Palace. Not Started.

The time is relative to the timezone you selected in Options. In this example, 16:00 is four o’clock in the afternoon. With the 12 hour choice, you would hear 4:00 PM.

You may receive fewer than three games. A tennis draw might not yet be complete, for example, or a team’s later fixtures may not have been announced. Dates and times can also change, so it is sensible to check again nearer the day.

Recent results and upcoming fixtures depend on the records available to the sports service. An empty list does not necessarily mean that a team has no fixtures or has never played. Try checking the name you entered and any team choice offered by Leasey.

Following hockey.

Hockey uses the same controls as the other sports. Once you know how to find a soccer or baseball game, there is no new set of commands to learn.

For example, to look for a Montreal Canadiens game:

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Hockey.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Events by date.

Step 5. Press Tab to Date.

Step 6. Type today.

Step 7. Press Tab to Keyword filter.

Step 8. Type Montreal Canadiens.

Step 9. Press Alt+F to search.

Step 10. Wait for focus to move to Results.

Step 11. Use Up or Down Arrow to read the games.

Step 12. Use Up or Down Arrow in Results to select a game in progress.

Step 13. Press Alt+C to check its score.

Step 14. Press Alt+M if you want regular updates through monitoring.

If there is no game today, try tomorrow:

Step 1. Press Alt+D to reach Date.

Step 2. Type tomorrow.

Step 3. Press Alt+F to search again.

You can also use “Finding a team’s or player’s next three games”.

To find hockey games being played now:

Step 1. Press Alt+A to reach Action.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Live scores.

Step 3. Press Tab to the keyword field.

Step 4. Type the team name, or press Backspace to clear the highlighted text for all live games.

Step 5. Press Enter to search.

Periods and other match information are included where available. Some competitions provide more detail than others.

Reading sports headlines.

Sports headlines are a convenient way to catch up with the wider news, including stories about games you have not been following. You can choose which country’s headlines you receive.

Choosing the country for your headlines.

Step 1. From the main window, press Control+Comma to open Options.

Step 2. Press Tab until you reach News country.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose United Kingdom, United States, Canada, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand.

Step 4. Press Tab until you reach the OK Button.

Step 5. Press Enter or Space.

Sports and Games remembers this choice for itself. If you previously chose a country in Leasey News, choose the country you want here as well.

Opening a news story.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+A to reach Action.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Sports news.

Step 3. Press Tab until you reach Find. Sports news does not need a date or team name.

Step 4. Press Enter or Space.

Step 5. Wait for the headlines to appear in Results.

Step 6. Use Up or Down Arrow to read them.

Step 7. Press Enter on a headline that interests you. The article opens in your web browser.

Step 8. Read the article using your usual JAWS browser commands.

Step 9. Press Alt+Tab when you want to return to the Sports and Games headlines.

Sports news covers general sports headlines for your chosen country. The Sport list does not limit the headlines to that sport. An article’s website may have its own sign-in or subscription arrangements.

Finding out more about a team or player.

You may know a team’s latest score but want to find out a little more about it. Team or player information can provide background facts and, where available, links to videos.

Let us look for information about West Ham United.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Soccer.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Team or player information.

Step 5. Press Tab to the keyword field.

Step 6. Type West Ham United.

Step 7. Press Enter to search.

Step 8. When focus moves to Results, use Up or Down Arrow to find Team or player information.

Step 9. Press Enter to open it.

Step 10. Read the Details field. The information varies, but may help you learn more about the club.

Step 11. Press Escape when you are ready to return to Results.

Step 12. If video links are listed, use Up or Down Arrow to choose one.

Step 13. If you selected a video link, press Enter to open it in your browser.

Step 14. Use Alt+Tab to return to Sports and Games afterwards.

You can follow the same procedure for a player by choosing the appropriate sport and entering the player’s name. You do not have to be following a live game to use this feature.

Reading about a team’s or player’s history.

For a longer article about a club or player, choose Team or player history. This searches Wikipedia and lets you read the available article text within Sports and Games.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+A to reach Action.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Team or player history.

Step 3. Press Tab to the keyword field.

Step 4. Enter a name, such as Liverpool Football Club.

Step 5. Press Enter to search.

Step 6. If Choose Wikipedia article appears, use Up or Down Arrow to find the article you want. Escape cancels the choice if none is suitable.

Step 7. If Choose Wikipedia article is open, press Enter to accept your choice.

Step 8. Wait for the article title to appear in Results.

Step 9. Press Enter to open it.

Step 10. Read the Details field using your usual reading commands.

Step 11. If you want a copy, press Tab until you reach Copy all.

Step 12. If you moved to Copy all, press Enter or Space to copy the text.

Step 13. Press Escape to return to Results.

Using a fuller name can make this search easier. Liverpool Football Club is more specific than Liverpool, which could also refer to the city. Historical articles are useful for background reading; use the score and fixture options for current game information.

Looking up league standings or tennis rankings.

After checking a result, you may wonder what it means for the league table. You can ask for the standings associated with a game in your Results list. The way you open a table, read its entries and return to your search is the same across the sports. The choices within the table depend on the competition. Tennis offers player rankings instead.

Let us start with a soccer example. We will find Liverpool’s most recent result, then look at the table for that game’s competition.

Step 1. Press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Soccer.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Most recent result.

Step 5. Press Alt+K to reach the keyword field. Existing text is highlighted.

Step 6. Type Liverpool to replace it.

Step 7. Press Alt+F to find the team.

Step 8. If a team choice appears, use Up or Down Arrow to select the team you want.

Step 9. If the team-choice dialogue is open, press Enter to accept your choice. When the game appears in Results, it is selected for you.

Step 10. Press Control+L to request the standings for that game’s competition and season.

Step 11. Wait for the standings entry to appear in Results. Its name includes the competition and season. A Premier League fixture should give Premier League in the name; a cup game may give another table or none.

Step 12. Press Enter to open the standings.

Choose the stage and group.

Continue here after opening the standings. A stage is a part of the competition, such as a regular season or pre-season. A group might be a whole league, a conference or a division. Conferences and divisions are named groups of teams within a competition.

For a simple league table there may be only one named group. You can keep All groups in that case.

Step 1. Check which control you have reached. Usually this is Group, with All groups selected. Some competitions offer Stage first.

Step 2. If focus is in Stage, use Up or Down Arrow to choose a stage. Regular season is selected initially when available.

Step 3. If you began in Stage, press Tab to Group.

Step 4. In Group, use Up or Down Arrow to choose All groups or a particular group.

Step 5. Press Tab to Teams.

Step 6. Use Up or Down Arrow to read the entries. Each gives its group and position, followed by the team and its main record. Soccer entries give points, wins, draws and losses.

Step 7. Press Enter on a team. Focus moves into a read-only Details field.

Step 8. Use the Arrow keys and your usual JAWS reading commands to read it. Soccer details include games played, goals for, goals against and goal difference, where supplied.

Step 9. Press Escape to close the details. You return to the same team.

Step 10. Press Escape again to close the standings window and return to Results.

Useful Tip: In these standings windows, Alt+G takes you to Group and Alt+T takes you to Teams. If Stage is present, Alt+S takes you to it. Alt+O opens the selected entry’s details. You can also press Tab to the Open details Button and press Enter or Space. To close the window using a button, press Tab until you reach the Close Button and press Enter or Space.

The standings replace the previous Results list. If you had used Events by date, Alt+Left Arrow brings back your last events list. Otherwise, you can run your earlier search again. Pressing Escape in the main window returns you to Sport.

Baseball, basketball and hockey.

These sports use the same method. For another example, use Chicago Cubs for baseball, Los Angeles Lakers for basketball or Montreal Canadiens for hockey.

Step 1. Press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose the sport.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Most recent result.

Step 5. Press Alt+K to reach the keyword field.

Step 6. Type the team name.

Step 7. Press Alt+F to search.

Step 8. If a team choice appears, use Up or Down Arrow to select the team.

Step 9. If that choice dialogue is open, press Enter to accept your choice.

Step 10. When the game appears in Results, press Control+L.

Step 11. Wait for the standings entry.

Step 12. Press Enter to open the table.

Continue with the stage and group choices below.

There are two useful points to bear in mind here. A team can belong to both a conference and a division. Also, a competition can supply separate pre-season and regular-season tables. Leasey keeps these distinctions so the records are easier to understand.

Step 1. If focus starts in Stage, use Up or Down Arrow to choose the stage. Basketball or hockey may offer NBA - Regular Season or NHL - Regular Season.

Step 2. Press Tab to Group after choosing a stage. If Stage is absent, focus is already in Group.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow in Group to choose a league, conference or division. For example, an NBA table may offer Eastern Conference, Western Conference and several divisions. An MLB table may offer American League, National League and their divisions. The choices come from the selected competition.

Step 4. Press Tab to Teams.

Step 5. Use Up or Down Arrow to review the records. Baseball and basketball give wins and losses. Hockey gives points, regulation wins and losses, and overtime wins and losses separately.

Step 6. Press Enter on a team to read its details. Baseball uses runs for and against; basketball uses points for and against; hockey uses goals for and against. These are different from the points used to place a team in a league table.

Step 7. Press Escape to return to the team.

Step 8. To choose another group, press Alt+G.

Step 9. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose the group.

Step 10. Press Tab to Teams again. Alt+S reaches Stage when that choice is available.

Step 11. Press Escape to close the standings window when you have finished.

With All groups selected, the same team can appear more than once. For example, you might hear a team in its conference table and again in its division table. Its position belongs to the group named at the start of that entry. Choosing one group makes it easier to follow just that table.

Cricket tables.

Cricket standings are available when the selected competition supplies a table. For example, the Indian Premier League supplies team points and net run rate. Some international matches and series have no table available through the service. In that case Leasey tells you, rather than presenting an empty list.

Step 1. Press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Cricket.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Most recent result.

Step 5. Press Alt+K to reach the keyword field.

Step 6. Type Chennai Super Kings as an example.

Step 7. Press Alt+F to search.

Step 8. If a team choice appears, use Up or Down Arrow to select Chennai Super Kings.

Step 9. If the team-choice dialogue is open, press Enter to accept your choice.

Open the cricket table.

Continue here after finding the team’s most recent result.

Step 1. When the game appears in Results, press Control+L.

Step 2. Wait for the standings entry.

Step 3. Press Enter to open it.

Step 4. If Stage is present, use Up or Down Arrow to choose a stage.

Step 5. Press Tab to Group after choosing a stage. If Stage is absent, begin in Group.

Step 6. Keep All groups, or use Up or Down Arrow to choose a supplied group.

Step 7. Press Tab to Teams.

Step 8. Use Up or Down Arrow to hear team points, wins and losses.

Step 9. Press Enter on a team to read its details. These may include games played, draws, games with no result and net run rate. Net run rate is supplied by the competition and can be positive or negative.

Step 10. Press Escape to return to Teams.

Step 11. Press Escape again to return to Results.

Tennis rankings.

For tennis, Control+L requests the service’s current ATP and WTA rankings. These are not the rankings from the date of the match you selected, and they are not the positions within that particular tournament.

Step 1. Press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Tennis.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Events by date.

Step 5. Press Tab to Date.

Step 6. Type today.

Step 7. Press Tab to the keyword field.

Step 8. Press Backspace to clear any highlighted text.

Step 9. Press Alt+F to search.

Step 10. Use Up or Down Arrow in Results to select a match.

Step 11. Press Control+L.

Step 12. Wait for the Tennis rankings entry.

Step 13. Press Enter to open it.

Read the tennis rankings.

Step 1. Focus is in Tour, with All tours selected. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose ATP or WTA if you want just one tour.

Step 2. Press Tab to Players.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow to review player positions and ranking points. Each entry names its tour.

Step 4. Press Enter on a player. The read-only details open.

Step 5. Use the Arrow keys to read them.

Step 6. Press Escape to return to the player list.

Step 7. If you want to change the tour, press Alt+T to reach Tour.

Step 8. If you moved to Tour, use Up or Down Arrow to choose the tour.

Step 9. If you changed the tour, press Tab to Players again. Alt+P is a shortcut to Players.

Step 10. Press Escape to close the rankings window and return to Results.

A few things common to these tables.

Changing Stage, Group or Tour uses the information already downloaded. It does not make another request or move focus away from the choice you are using. To request a fresh table, close the standings window, find a game again and press Control+L. If your original search was Events by date, Alt+Left Arrow can return you to that events list first.

Team standings belong to the competition and season of the selected game. The season appears in the window title and the team’s details. A basketball season, for example, may be shown as 2026-2027. Missing figures are described as unavailable, rather than being treated as zero. The sports service determines which tables and records are available.

Press Insert+F1 for help with the control you are using. Review the Leasey Help text with the arrow keys and press Escape to return. Leasey Command Centre and Where Am I are available in these windows too.

American football uses the same list and details approach, with Conference as its filter. The next section takes you through NFL and college examples.

NFL and college football standings.

Perhaps you follow the Buffalo Bills and would like to know how they are doing alongside other NFL teams. Or you may be interested in a college team and want to concentrate on its conference. A conference is a group of teams within the competition. The NFL has two conferences, AFC and NFC, with smaller divisions within each one. College conferences include the Big Ten and Southeastern Conference.

You can review all the available teams or choose one conference. There is no need to wait for a game to be in progress. A completed game can also be used to reach its competition’s standings.

Looking at the NFL standings.

Let us use the Buffalo Bills as an example.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose American football.

Step 3. Press Alt+A to reach Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Most recent result.

Step 5. Press Tab to the team or player field. Existing text is highlighted.

Step 6. Type Buffalo Bills.

Step 7. Press Enter to search.

Step 8. If a team choice appears, use Up or Down Arrow to select Buffalo Bills.

Step 9. If the choice dialogue is open, press Enter to accept your choice. If no choice was needed, wait for the result.

Step 10. Wait for focus to move to Results. You should hear a game involving the Bills.

Step 11. With that game selected, press Control+L.

Step 12. Wait for the standings entry in Results. Its name includes NFL standings and the season.

Step 13. Press Enter to open it.

Read the NFL table.

Step 1. From Conference, which begins with All conferences selected, press Tab to Teams.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to read the entries. All conferences includes the available NFL teams, grouped by conference and division.

You might hear an entry beginning, “AFC East. Position 1. Buffalo Bills.” This is followed by their overall wins, losses and ties. The position belongs to that division; it is not a position among all NFL teams. The records and positions will naturally change as the season progresses.

Step 3. To concentrate on one conference, press Shift+Tab to Conference.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose AFC or NFC. Teams updates, while focus stays in Conference.

Step 5. Press Tab to Teams.

Step 6. Use Up or Down Arrow to review the filtered list.

Step 7. Press Enter on a team. Focus moves to its read-only Details field.

Step 8. Use Up or Down Arrow to read the competition, season, conference, division and overall record.

Step 9. Press Escape to return to the same team in the list.

Step 10. To include every team again, press Shift+Tab to Conference.

Step 11. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose All conferences.

Step 12. Press Tab to return to Teams.

Step 13. Press Escape to close the standings window and return to Results.

Useful Tip: Within the standings window, Alt+C takes you to Conference and Alt+T takes you to Teams. Alt+O opens the selected team’s details. You can also press Tab to the Open details Button and press Enter or Space.

Looking at college standings.

For college football, we can use Ohio State as an example. The procedure is very similar, but college teams have their own conferences and records.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose American football.

Step 3. Press Alt+A to reach Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Most recent result.

Step 5. Press Tab to the team or player field.

Step 6. Type Ohio State.

Step 7. Press Enter to search.

Step 8. If a team choice appears, use Up or Down Arrow to select Ohio State.

Step 9. If the choice dialogue is open, press Enter to accept your choice.

Step 10. When the game appears in Results, press Control+L.

Step 11. Wait for the College football standings entry.

Step 12. Press Enter to open it.

Read the college table.

Step 1. In Conference, use Up or Down Arrow to choose Big Ten for Ohio State’s conference. All conferences is selected initially.

Step 2. Press Tab to Teams.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow to review the teams. Each entry names its college competition and conference, then gives its overall record and conference record.

The overall record includes the team’s games across the season. The conference record covers games within its conference. The figures can therefore differ.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to select a team.

Step 5. Press Enter to open its details.

Step 6. Read the details with the Arrow keys.

Step 7. Press Escape to return to the same team.

Step 8. Press Shift+Tab to Conference.

Step 9. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose another conference, or All conferences.

Step 10. Press Tab to Teams.

Step 11. Review the list. All conferences includes every college team supplied in this table. Competition names distinguish different college levels where these are included.

Step 12. Press Escape to return to Results.

College positions are within the conference or division named in the entry. This is not the Associated Press Top 25 poll, and it is not a playoff qualification list. If a record is missing from the sports service, Leasey says that it is unavailable rather than treating it as zero.

A few useful points about these tables.

The standings use the competition and season of the game you selected. The season is included in the standings window’s title and in each team’s details. A playoff game played in January can belong to the season which began the previous year.

Changing Conference uses the table already downloaded. It does not repeatedly check the sports service. To request a fresh table, close the standings window, find a game again and press Control+L. If your original search was Events by date, you can return to that events list with Alt+Left Arrow first.

Press Insert+F1 for help with the control you are using. Read the Leasey Help text with the arrow keys and press Escape to return. Leasey Command Centre and Where Am I are also available in the standings window.

Saving a favourite search.

If you often look for the same team, a favourite saves some typing. For example, you could save an Events by date search for Liverpool and use it whenever you want to see whether they are playing today.

A favourite remembers the sport, action and keyword. It remembers what to search for, rather than keeping an old set of results.

Saving your search.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Soccer.

Step 3. Press Tab to Action.

Step 4. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Events by date.

Step 5. Press Tab to Date.

Step 6. Type today.

Step 7. Press Tab to the keyword field.

Step 8. Type Liverpool. You can press Enter to run the search first if you want to check the choices.

Step 9. Press Alt+V to open View.

Step 10. Use Up or Down Arrow to find Save current search as favourite.

Step 11. Press Enter on that menu item. You should hear:

Favourite saved.

If you have already saved the same search, Leasey tells you that it is already saved.

Using a favourite.

Step 1. From the main window, press Control+B to open Favourites.

Step 2. Use Up or Down Arrow to read your saved searches. Each description includes the sport, action and keyword so that you can recognise it.

Step 3. Press Enter on the one you want. Press Escape instead if you decide not to run a search.

Step 4. If a team or article list opens, use Up or Down Arrow to select the entry you want.

Step 5. If the choice dialogue is open, press Enter to accept your choice.

Step 6. When focus moves to Results, use Up or Down Arrow to read the entries.

Step 7. Press Enter to open an entry.

Step 8. Press Escape to close its details.

An Events by date favourite always searches for today; it does not keep the date that was entered when you saved it. You can save other actions too, such as a team’s next three games.

Saving or choosing a favourite does not start monitoring. To follow a live game automatically, or queue a scheduled game for its start time, press Alt+R to reach Results, select it with Up or Down Arrow and press Alt+M. There are no separate controls for renaming or deleting favourites.

Returning to an events list.

You may have looked up the league table or read some team information and now want to go back to the events you were browsing.

Step 1. If a details dialogue is open, press Escape to return to the main window.

Step 2. Press Alt+Left Arrow.

Step 3. Your last Events by date results return, with focus in the Results list. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose a game.

This brings back the most recent events list from the current visit to Sports and Games. It does not fetch newer scores. For an update, use Up or Down Arrow to select a game, then press Alt+C. The list is not kept after you close the application.

Running a search again.

To fetch a new set of results, press Alt+F to activate Find.

Step 1. Press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Listen to the current sport.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow if you want to change it.

Step 4. Press Tab to Action.

Step 5. Listen to the current action.

Step 6. Use Up or Down Arrow if you want to change it.

Step 7. Press Tab to Date, when it is available.

Step 8. Check or replace the highlighted date as needed.

Step 9. Press Tab to the keyword field, when it is available.

Step 10. Check or replace the highlighted search text as needed.

Step 11. Press Alt+F to search.

Step 12. Wait for the new results.

Step 13. Read them with Up or Down Arrow.

To use the Find Button instead of Alt+F:

Step 1. Press Tab until you reach Find.

Step 2. Press Enter or Space.

Alt+F uses the choices currently in the search controls. This is helpful to remember after using Last events, because bringing an old list back does not also change those controls back to their earlier values.

Changing a sport or action does not start a new search by itself. Until you press Alt+F and the new search finishes, any old results still on screen belong to your previous search.

Hiding the window and coming back to it.

You can leave Sports and Games open while using other applications. If you would like to put its window away, use the Hide or restore shortcut. The application continues running in the system tray, the Windows area for icons belonging to background applications.

Hiding Sports and Games.

Step 1. If a details, Options or Monitored games dialogue is open, press Escape to close it. If another dialogue remains underneath, press Escape again until you are back in the main window. Escape in Options cancels any unsaved changes.

Step 2. Press the Hide or restore shortcut. Its initial setting is Control+Alt+G.

Step 3. Continue with your other work. If you were monitoring games, the checks continue. If you had paused monitoring, it remains paused.

Moving to another application or using Windows+D to show the desktop does not send Sports and Games to the system tray. It remains available through normal Windows window switching, including Alt+Tab. Windows may minimise windows when showing the desktop, but Sports and Games does not turn that into a hide-to-tray command. Use the Hide or restore shortcut when you want to put the app in the tray. Escape anywhere in the main search window returns you to Sport, just like Alt+S. Your search fields, results and monitoring are kept.

Bringing the window back.

Step 1. Press the Hide or restore shortcut again, initially Control+Alt+G.

Step 2. Sports and Games returns to the foreground. You can continue with the controls or press Control+M to review your monitored games.

The shortcut works while the application is running. If you closed it completely, use the Leasey Key followed by Shift+G to open it again.

You can also use the Sports and Games icon in the system tray, the Windows area for background applications. Its menu offers Open Sports and Games, Monitored games, Pause monitoring, Reinstate session and Exit.

Closing Sports and Games completely.

Step 1. If a dialogue is open, press Escape to close it. If another dialogue remains underneath, press Escape again until you are back in the main window. Escape in Options cancels any unsaved changes.

Step 2. Press Alt+F4. Control+Q has the same effect.

Step 3. Sports and Games closes, and its score checking stops. Your choices and saved games are kept for your next visit.

Alt+F4 normally closes the window you are currently working in. If you use it in a details dialogue, for example, it closes that dialogue. Use it in the main window when you want to leave Sports and Games altogether.

Choosing your own shortcuts.

The Hide or restore and Show scores shortcuts can be used while you are working in another application. Their initial settings are Control+Alt+G and Control+Shift+S, but you can choose combinations that suit you better.

The Options dialogue contains an Edit Field for each shortcut. You type the name of the combination into the field. For example, to choose Control, Shift and G, you type this text:

CTRL+Shift+G.

You do not hold those three keys down to enter the setting. Type the letters and plus signs, just as you would type a word.

Step 1. In the main window, press Control+Comma to open Options.

Step 2. Press Tab until you reach Hide or restore shortcut. Its existing text is highlighted.

Step 3. Type the combination you want, such as CTRL+Shift+G. If you want to keep the current shortcut, leave its text unchanged.

Step 4. Press Tab to Show scores shortcut. Its text is highlighted.

Step 5. If you want to change it, type a different combination from Hide or restore. Otherwise, keep the existing text.

Step 6. Press Tab until you reach the OK Button.

Step 7. Press Enter or Space.

If a shortcut cannot be saved.

Step 1. If Leasey reports that a combination is already in use or invalid, press Enter or Space on the message’s OK Button.

Step 2. In Options, press Shift+Tab until you reach the shortcut field you want to change.

Step 3. Type another combination over the highlighted text.

Step 4. Press Tab until you reach OK.

Step 5. Press Enter or Space to try saving again.

You can use Ctrl, Alt and Shift with a letter, a number, or a function key from F1 to F12. Include Ctrl or Alt in each combination. For example, Control+Alt+F8 is suitable in form, but Shift+G on its own is not. Capital letters and lowercase letters are both accepted.

Choose combinations that will not interfere with JAWS commands or shortcuts you already use. Once you change one, use your chosen combination wherever this chapter mentions the initial setting.

These two shortcuts control the running application. The Leasey Key followed by Shift+G remains the command for opening Sports and Games through Leasey.

If the information you expected is not there.

Sports information can take a little time to catch up with play, and not every competition provides the same level of detail. A missing score does not always mean that you have entered something incorrectly.

Here are a few useful things to check before trying again.

A game or team is missing from the results.

Step 1. In the main window, press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 2. Listen to the current sport.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow to correct it if necessary.

Step 4. Press Tab to Action.

Step 5. Listen to the current action.

Step 6. Use Up or Down Arrow to correct it if necessary.

Step 7. For Events by date, press Tab to Date.

Step 8. Listen to the date.

Step 9. Type a different date over the highlighted text if necessary. Dates follow the timezone chosen in Options.

Step 10. Press Alt+K to reach the keyword field.

Step 11. Listen to its contents. A filter left from an earlier search may be narrowing the results.

Step 12. Press Backspace on the highlighted text if you want to clear the filter.

Step 13. Press Alt+F to search again.

Step 14. If the game has only just begun, allow time for it to be reported as live.

Step 15. Press Alt+F to search again after waiting.

For a team or player search, another option is to press Alt+K and enter a shorter name before searching. If matching names appear, use Up or Down Arrow to choose the one you want, then press Enter.

If a search fails, the earlier results can remain in the list. Listen to any error message before treating those entries as the results of your new search.

You have not heard a score update for a while.

Step 1. Use Alt+Tab to return to Sports and Games. If you hid it, use your Hide or restore shortcut, initially Control+Alt+G.

Step 2. From the main window, press Control+M to open Monitored games.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow to review the saved games. Make sure the game you want is still there.

Step 4. Press Alt+C to activate Check now and ask for the latest scores. If the score and stage of play are unchanged, there may have been nothing new to announce.

Step 5. If you deliberately paused the session and want to resume, press Tab until you reach Reinstate.

Step 6. If you chose to resume the paused session, press Enter or Space on Reinstate. Automatic checks resume. A previously active session resumes automatically when the app reopens.

Step 7. Press Escape to close Monitored games.

Step 8. Press Control+H if you want to review earlier announcements.

Step 9. If you opened Announcement history, read it with Up or Down Arrow.

Step 10. Press Escape to return to the main window.

If a check fails because the connection or sports service is unavailable, Leasey keeps the last known score and tries again later. It does not remove a game just because it could not obtain an update. If you know the game has ended but it is still being followed, you can remove it using the steps under Stopping just one game.

If the service asks you to wait before checking again, allow it some time. Repeatedly pressing Check now will not make the information arrive sooner. If a problem continues, note the sport, team, action you were using and the message you heard when asking for help.

Recording information to help investigate a problem.

If monitoring seems to stop reporting changes, you may be asked to turn on monitoring diagnostics. This keeps a quiet record of the checks and the information returned by the sports service. It can help show whether Leasey is having trouble getting information, or whether the reported score has stayed the same.

Step 1. From the main window, press Control+Comma to open Options.

Step 2. Press Tab until you reach Enable monitoring diagnostics. It is initially unchecked.

Step 3. Check its current state.

Step 4. Press Space if you need to check it.

Step 5. Press Tab until you reach the OK Button.

Step 6. Press Enter or Space. Diagnostics now records while you use the app. It does not add spoken messages or change how you navigate.

Step 7. Follow the game as usual. If the problem occurs, note approximately when you noticed it.

Save a diagnostic copy.

Step 1. Press Control+Comma to open Options again.

Step 2. Press Tab until you reach Save diagnostics.

Step 3. Press Enter or Space. The standard Windows Save As dialogue opens.

Step 4. Choose the folder for the copy in Save As.

Step 5. Choose a filename. The suggested name is SportsAndGamesDiagnostics.txt.

Step 6. Press Tab until you reach Save.

Step 7. Press Enter or Space. You hear Diagnostics saved when the copy is ready.

The copy is not sent anywhere automatically. You can provide it to the person helping you investigate. It contains details of the games and checks, but excludes API keys, the private codes used to access a service. The working log is limited in size, so save a copy soon after noticing the problem.

Turn diagnostics off.

Step 1. When recording is no longer needed, return to Options.

Step 2. Press Tab until you reach Enable monitoring diagnostics.

Step 3. Check whether it is checked.

Step 4. Press Space if you need to uncheck it.

Step 5. Press Tab until you reach OK.

Step 6. Press Enter or Space. Copies already saved remain available.

The working diagnostic file is stored at:

C:\LeaseyData\SportsAndGames\Diagnostics\monitoring.log.

If the app cannot save the monitoring session, it clearly announces that automatic monitoring has stopped. The message is also sent to Braille and kept in Announcement history for the current session, even if the settings file cannot be written. After resolving the saving problem, use Reinstate to continue.

Remembering your choices.

Sports and Games saves your timezone, time format, news country, checking interval, sound and speech choices, shortcuts, filters and favourites. It also keeps the monitoring session and recent announcement history.

For example, after searching for Liverpool’s upcoming games, you can return to that search without typing Liverpool again.

Step 1. Open Sports and Games.

Step 2. Press Alt+S to reach Sport.

Step 3. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Soccer.

Step 4. Press Tab to Action.

Step 5. Use Up or Down Arrow to choose Next three games.

Step 6. Press Tab to the keyword field. Liverpool is already there and highlighted.

Step 7. If you want a different team, type its name to replace Liverpool.

Step 8. Press Enter to search.

Each sport keeps its own last search text. Looking up a hockey team does not replace Liverpool under Soccer. If you clear the field and search for all events or live scores, that empty field is remembered too. Reading sports news does not change the saved search text.

You do not need to enter these choices again each time you open the application. An active monitoring session resumes automatically after reopening. If you deliberately paused it, that choice is remembered; press Control+R in the main window when you want the announcements to resume.

Keystroke summary.

You can return to this section whenever you need a reminder. Insert+F1 opens Leasey Help for the control you are using. For the general keyboard reference, press Alt+H in the main window to open the Help menu. Use Up or Down Arrow to find Keyboard help and press Enter. Press Escape to close either reading window.

Opening the application and using it from other programs.

- Leasey Key, then Shift+G: open Sports and Games.

- Control+Alt+G initially: hide or restore the running application. You can change this in Options.

- Control+Shift+S initially: bring the running application forward, check your saved games and open Monitored games. You can change this in Options.

Moving around and entering information.

- Tab: move to the next available control.

- Shift+Tab: move to the previous control.

- Up Arrow and Down Arrow: move through the choices in a list.

- Typing when you enter an Edit Field: replace the highlighted text.

- Backspace when you enter an Edit Field: clear the highlighted text.

- Left Arrow and Right Arrow in an Edit Field: move within the text to read or edit it.

- Control+A in an Edit Field: highlight all the text again if you have moved the cursor within it.

- Space on a checkbox: change whether it is checked.

- Enter or Space on a button: activate it.

Searching and reading results in the main window.

- Alt+S: move to Sport.

- Alt+A: move to Action.

- Alt+D: move to Date, when available.

- Alt+K: move to the keyword field, when available.

- Enter in a search field: start the search.

- Enter or Space on the Find Button: start the search.

- Alt+F: run the search shown in the current controls again.

- Alt+R: move to Results.

- Enter in Results, or Alt+O: open the selected details, article or link.

- Alt+C: check the selected game’s score.

- Alt+M: monitor the selected live game, or queue a scheduled game for its start time.

- Left Arrow and Right Arrow in a list box: review the previous or next virtual column.

- Alt+Home and Alt+End in a list box: review the first or last virtual column.

- Alt+Up Arrow and Alt+Down Arrow in a list box: review the same column in the previous or next item.

- Control+L: request standings for the selected game’s competition, or tennis rankings.

- Control+B: choose a favourite search.

- Alt+Left Arrow: bring back the last Events by date results from this visit.

- Control+Comma: open Options.

- Insert+F1: open Leasey Help for the current control. Use Up or Down Arrow to read it and Escape to return.

- Control+Shift+C, or Insert+H through Leasey: open Leasey Command Centre.

- Control+Shift+I: hear a short description of your current position with Where Am I.

Managing monitoring.

- Control+M in the main window: open Monitored games.

- Control+P in the main window: pause monitoring and keep your saved games.

- Control+R in the main window: reinstate the saved session.

- Control+Shift+R in the main window: check the saved games now.

- Control+H in the main window: open Announcement history.

- Alt+C in Monitored games: activate Check now for saved games whose start time has arrived.

- Alt+D in Monitored games, or Enter in its list: open the selected game’s details.

- Alt+P in Monitored games: pause automatic checks while keeping the session.

- Delete in the Monitored games list: ask to remove the selected game, with confirmation.

In Monitored games, the buttons are Check now, Details, Remove, Pause, Reinstate and Close. Press Tab until JAWS announces the button you want, then press Enter or Space. The Close Button returns to the main window without changing whether monitoring is running or paused.

Closing a dialog or leaving the application.

- Escape in a details, help, choice or Options dialogue: close or cancel the dialogue.

- Escape anywhere in the main search window: return to Sport, just like Alt+S, keeping your search fields, results and monitoring.

- Alt+F4 or Control+Q in the main window: close Sports and Games and stop its checks.

Use the main-window shortcuts after pressing Escape to close any open dialogue. If another dialogue remains underneath, press Escape again to return to the main window. While you are in Monitored games, for example, its Pause and Reinstate buttons provide those actions directly.

Leasey Spotify

Introduction.

Spotify gives you millions of songs at your fingertips. The artists you love, the latest hits, and new discoveries just for you. It allows you to stream songs over the internet and listen to them as if they were stored on your computer. Imagine being let loose in a music store with permission to play anything you want, old and new. You can play any song, any time! There are also hundreds of playlists other people have created to suit any mood or music genre. Why search for songs when someone else has done the work? Whether you want to relax, have music to exercise to or hear the latest hits, Spotify has you covered.

Sometimes only your favourite artist will do. You can play all their music on shuffle, for free. There are two types of Spotify account, ‘Free’ and ‘Premium’. Among other considerations, ‘Spotify Premium’ allows you to play all the music you want without the interruption of commercials. If you enjoy listening to music, particularly albums in their entirety, it is worthwhile purchasing a monthly subscription to ‘Spotify Premium’ for this useful addition alone.

Signing Up for a Spotify Account.

Even if you wish to use ‘Spotify Free’, this does require the creation of an account. Visiting the website at www.spotify.com will allow you to create one.

There are two ways in which an account can be created. The first is to log in with your Facebook cridentials if you have a Facebook account. If this is selected, then many of your details will be retrieved from your Facebook profile directly. This includes your Facebook Email address and password. You will use the Email address as your username.

The recommended option however is to create an account using your Email address, since you will be able to choose the username and password in order to use Spotify. The password can be something which is memorable to you.

When the account is created on the Spotify website, you can then elect to choose ‘Spotify Premium’, submitting your credit card information. Indeed the company may give you a trial of ‘Spotify Premium’ at no cost if you would like to evaluate the experience.

When Spotify loads, you will be asked for your username and password. With Leasey installed, it is not necessary to enter ‘Forms Mode’.

Step 1. Focus is automatically set to the ‘Username’ field. Please type it in and press Tab.

Step 2. Type the password for your account and press Enter.

  • Note that if you press Tab rather than Enter, focus will now be set to a Check Box. At the time of writing, it is not possible to toggle this Check Box by pressing the Space Bar and the status is always reported as being ‘Unchecked’. The purpose of the Check Box is to allow automatic log into Spotify each time it is started. However by default, the Check Box is set to allow automatic log in, so press Tab once more.
  • You are now on the ‘Sign In’ Button. Press the Space Bar, not Enter, on this Button.

You should now be logged into Spotify. press Insert+T which will cause JAWS to announce the account type you have access to, such as ‘Spotify Free’ or ‘Spotify Premium’. If JAWS announces ‘Spotify’, you are not logged in.

Using Spotify.

Having logged into Spotify, we can now begin to find music to listen to!

When working through the rest of the tasks in this Chapter, please pay particular attention to the instructions and carry them out precisely in order that Leasey Spotify will work correctly for you.

To the average user, Spotify appears as a series of web pages. So any techniques you have learned in order to browse content on the internet can be used here, together with the additional keystrokes and methods of navigation which will be detailed below. Pay particular attention to moving by Heading (by pressing the letter “H”), accessing a list of Links (Insert+F7), and using the JAWS Find facility (Control+F).

Searching for Songs.

Let us start with a simple task, searching for a song. Working through this procedure should introduce you to the concept is a good training ground.

There are two methods in respect of searching for a song. There is a method you can use from within Leasey Search, or alternatively, the more traditional way. If you are using the Leasey Search method, Spotify does not need to be running at this point. However, we will first relate the traditional method.

Step 1. Press Control+Shift+F to find a song.

Step 2. Type a song title such as ‘Thinking Out Loud’.

Step 3. Press Enter.

Step 4. The search is carried out and in a second or two you should be focused upon the first search result. JAWS will speak the title of the song assuming it exists.

Step 5. Focus is now in a list of results. You can press the Down Arrow key to review them. First you will see what Spotify deems to be the “Top Result”, followed by a list of the most popular songs matching the search criteria.

Song Details.

As you press the Down Arrow key to move through the songs which have been found, you are likely to discover a number of elements.

  • A Button inviting you to play the song.
  • The song name as plain text.
  • A hyperlink to the artist. Pressing Enter on this item will take you to the artist page from where you can view their catalogue.
  • A Button to save the song to your library.
  • The length of the song.
  • A Button entitled “More”. Activating this Button will reveal options such as to share the item, add it to your playlist, and more. We will return to this later.

Press Enter on any of the Buttons to perform the desired action.

Note that when songs are playing, you can use the following keystrokes to control the playback.

  • Pause and Play Song, Alt+Control+Windows+P.
  • Volume Up, Alt+Control+Windows+Up Arrow.
  • Volume Down, Alt+Control+Windows+Down Arrow.
  • Next Track, Control+Shift+N.
  • Previous Track, Control+Shift+P.
  • Fast Forward, Alt+Control+Windows+Right Arrow.
  • Rewind, Alt+Control+Windows+Left Arrow.
  • Toggle Shuffle, Control+S.
  • Toggle Repeat, Control+R.

Browsing Around.

Within this Chapter, we are going to describe some specific strategies you can use to get the most from Spotify when reading the pages. However, you may wish to explore the individual pages yourself, given that it has been made very accessible for you in the most part. You can read any of the text on the pages and activate the Links and Buttons in order to move to different sections of Spotify.

Here are some useful tips when navigating:

Press Enter on any Link or Button, not the Space Bar.

Use the list of Links, (Insert+F7), for fast navigation through sections.

When focused on a new page, press Control+Shift+R (for ‘Results’), and Leasey will try to set focus to the starting point of the text on the page, bypassing any repeated Links or sections at the top.

Press the letter ‘H’ to move through Headings if needed.

  • While every attempt has been made to instruct JAWS to refresh the new page when it is loaded, particularly with older versions of JAWS this is not always achieved. If you have loaded a new page and you feel that the text displayed is not what you expect to see, press Insert+Escape to refresh the Virtual Buffer, then try reading the page again.
  • You can listen to songs continuously in Spotify while safely navigating to other sections. Playback will not stop unless you choose to terminate it.

To move back to the previous page, press Alt+Left Arrow.

To move to the Spotify ‘Home Page’, press Control+Shift+H.

If you wish to search for a word or phrase on the page, press Control+F.

Using Leasey Search to Find Items on Spotify.

This method is useful if you quickly want to find a song on Spotify and you may not have the application running or if you wish to locate an item fairly quickly. The concept is that you will find the item in a List Box, press Enter, and the relevant page on Spotify will be loaded into the application. You will then need to do a little work in order to begin playing the item.

Step 1. Move into Leasey Search by pressing the Leasey Key then Control+Shift+S.

Step 2. Select Spotify and press Enter. If the Spotify application is already in focus, you can go straight to this method of search by pressing Control+Shift+S without the Leasey Key.

Step 3. Type a song title and press Enter. Note it is important to be as specific as you can if possible, so if you are searching for a song, include the artist or group name to ensure the results are to your taste. You could also type an artist or group name by itself, or with the album name, etc.

Step 4. A list of results will be displayed. Press Down Arrow to find the result you want. Note that the list contains anything Spotify holds including this term, such as songs, albums or playlists with this title. Find something which may interest you by pressing Down Arrow and press Enter. If you have searched for a song, and you have entered the artist or group name as well, in the vast majority of cases the first result will be the one you want.

Step 5. The Spotify application will then run if it was not previously launched and the page for the item will be available. Hopefully, the song will begin to play if that is what you have searched for and focus should be on the “Pause” Button.

Step 6. Now you should use any browsing techniques discussed above.

Step 7. To return to your search results list, you can press the Leasey Key then Alt+Left Arrow.

Selecting an Artist.

You will have noticed while browsing the list of results in our song search that the artists are displayed as Hyperlinks. You can press enter on any one of the Links so as to display the artist page. Press Insert+T to verify that the artist page is loaded and you should find the name of the artist reflected there.

Having done this, press number 2 on the keyboard, above the letter keys. This takes you to the first level 2 heading where the results start, whereupon you can explore the page. This is usually under Spotify’s Heading of ‘Popular’, meaning that they are played by users more frequently. If you want to examine songs under this Heading, Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to review the available options.

If on the other hand you wish to move through albums of the artist selected, press H to move through the Headings. Each album is denoted by a hyperlink. Press Enter to move to the album page. Again, the window title reflects the album which has been selected.

Moving to the first table by pressing the letter T will show all the tracks on the album. The layout is a very similar arrangement to search results, except that the items also contain statistical data, such as the number of times the item has been played. You can press the Space Bar on any item to play it.

You will find just above the songs listed on the album details of the number of tracks, the total playing time and, crucially, a Button labelled “Save”. Pressing Enter on this Button will save the album to “Your Music” if desired.

Selecting Playlists.

We will now introduce you to the concept of Playlists. Playlists are a compilation of tracks a person has prepared, usually to reflect a particular musical style. These can make for good listening and, if you are not tempted to look at the track list, you can get a surprise when you listen to the music and perhaps one of your favourites is played. ‘Shuffle Mode’ is also very appealing when listening to music in a Playlist.

From the Home Page, the easiest way to find your Playlists is to press the letter B to reach the Button “Create a Playlist”. Just below this you will find your Playlists with each one denoted by a hyperlink. Press Enter to move into it. However, if you explore the home page, you will find plenty of Playlists advertised for you based on those songs you have played recently.

When you find a Playlist you would like to hear, press Enter on the Link containing its name.

When inside a Playlist, there are a number of things you can do:

Step 1. Press Control+Home to move to the top of the page.

Step 2. Press letter “H” to move to the first Level 1 Heading which is the Playlist title.

Step 3. Press Down Arrow to read the page. You will first find a ‘Play Pause’ Button. Press Enter to play all the songs from the beginning or in a random order of ‘Shuffle Mode’ is on.

Step 4. Next comes a ‘Follow’ Button. If you are already following the Playlist, you will hear the word ‘Following’. Press Enter to unfollow or conversely, if you are not following the Playlist and you would like to do so, press Enter to follow it.

Step 5. Next comes the name of the Playlist creator, the total number of songs and the running time.

Step 6. The results are displayed in a table, so you can always move straight to this by pressing the letter “T”.

Step 7. If browsing through the results, you can play a track by placing the cursor on the “Play” Button relative to the track and pressing Enter. But in most cases, the purpose of selecting a Playlist is to hear a collection of songs and to enjoy them!

Creating Your Own Playlists and an Introduction to the Context Menu.

For each individual music track you search for, it is possible to activate a Context Menu so as to interact with it. You can add the song to a Playlist, start a radio station playing based on the track, add it to the playing queue, and more. In this section, we will work through how to use the Context Menu.

Before we do this, we need to create a new Playlist.

Step 1. From any Spotify page, press the letter “B” repeatedly until you reach a Button entitled “Create New Playlist”.

Step 2. Press Enter on the Button, (or press Control+N), and an Edit Field will be in focus.

Step 3. If necessary, activate Forms Mode by pressing Enter. Type the name of the Playlist into the Edit Field. We will use the title “Leasey” as our example.

Step 4. Press Tab to reach the “Create” Playlist” Button and press Enter. You will note that there is a field for adding a description. This is optional.

Step 5. Our Playlist is now created. We will add a song to it. Press Control+Shift+F and type a song title you know to be on Spotify. When this is done, press Enter. Alternatively you can use the Leasey Search method of access.

Step 6. After a short pause, you will be placed within the search results. Press the Up or Down Arrow keys until the song you wish to add is spoken.

Step 7. Press Enter on the appropriate Button to play it. This is for two reasons: first because you can determine if it is the correct version and second because this loads up the appropriate song or album page.

Step 8. Press letter “B” to reach the “More Options For” Button and press Enter. Tip: If you do not find this Button right away, it could be that the Button is not visually available. To work around this issue, press Control+End to move to the bottom of the page and press Shift+B repeatedly. Then press Enter.

Step 9. You are now in a Context Menu. Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to find the item “Add to Playlist” and press Enter.

Step 10. A list of your Playlists is displayed. Move to the name of the Playlist by pressing Down Arrow. In our example, this is, “Leasey”.

Step 11. Press Enter, and the song is now in the Playlist. JAWS says “Added to Playlist”.

Note that if you wish to add other songs, you should repeat the procedure.

To be thorough, we should check that the song is in the Playlist, however when adding multiple songs it is unlikely you will carry out this process. It is worth describing however because at some point, you are going to want to listen to it.

Step 1. From the Home Page, press the letter “B” until you reach the Button “Create a Playlist”.

Step 2. Press Down Arrow, and you will find all your Playlists. Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to move through the available Playlists. When you reach one you would like to select, press Enter.

Step 3. The procedure for listening to the content of the playlist is exactly the same as that which we have already explored. In summary, press the letter “T” to reach the table of song titles and locate the song.

Step 4. Underneath the Playlist title is a “Play Pause” Button. Press Enter to listen to the songs in the Playlist.

Step 5. If you wish to activate the Context menu for the playlist, Press Enter on the “More” Button for it.

Step 6. Press Down Arrow to move through the options on the Context Menu. The options include:

  • Start Playlist Radio. Starts a radio station based upon the content of the Playlist, containing similar songs to those listed.
  • Share. Allows the sharing of the Playlist on social media. This includes copying the URI to the Clipboard. This is a link which can be shared in order that anyone can listen to it on Spotify.
  • Copy Playlist Link. Copies a Link to the clipboard of the Playlist which can be shared with someone else, perhaps in an Email. When the second user activates the Link, the Spotify web player will load in the browser, and will play the songs in the Playlist.
  • Collaborative Playlist. Activating this option means you can then copy the Playlist URI (as above), and send it to a friend. When he or she opens the Playlist in Spotify, songs can be added, with them being available then to you and your friend.
  • Make Secret or Make Public. This is simple. If made secret, the Playlist is not visible to the public. If Make Public is selected, it will be available to everyone potentially.
  • Rename. Allows you to rename the Playlist. An Edit Field is made instantly available. Edit the existing name, or type a new one, then press Enter.
  • Delete. This displays a new window with a “Delete” Button at the bottom of the page. Press Control+End, and you should be focused on the “Delete” Button. Press Enter to remove the Playlist.

Step 7. To activate an item on the Context Menu, press Enter.

Deleting a Song from a Playlist.

If you wish to delete a song from a playlist:

Step 1. Be sure you are located on the Playlist page as described in the previous section.

Step 2. Use the Up and Down Arrow keys to move to the song you wish to delete.

Step 3. Press Enter to play the song to be sure it is the correct one.

Step 4. Press Alt+Control+Shift+P to pause the playback.

Step 5. Find the “More Options” Button underneath the song and press Enter to activate the Context Menu.

Step 6. When the Context Menu is displayed, press Down Arrow until you reach “Remove from Playlist”.

Step 7. Press Enter to remove the song from the Playlist.

Context Menu Items Relating to Tracks.

We have already explored the Context Menu relating to tracks, as we used it to add to our Playlist. However, there are other items on the Context Menu which are useful. These are very similar to the options we’ve just worked through when exploring a Context Menu for the Playlist. However, we have not covered:

  • Add to Queue. If you are listening to a song, and you have a sudden need to hear a piece of music which comes into your mind, you can find the song on Spotify and use this menu item to add to the playing queue. It will be played when the currently playing song finishes.
  • Start Song Radio. This is similar to the above option in relation to a Playlist, except that a radio station will be created based upon the selected song. This is excellent as it introduces you to new music of a similar genre.

Sharing a Track or Playlist With Others.

You may talk about music with your friends and family. They may well be Spotify users and hear songs you might enjoy. Now, they can send you Links to songs or Playlists they may have created and you can listen to them. How cool is that?

As we briefly described earlier, Spotify contains what is known as a “U R I”. This is a Link pointing to a music track or Playlist on Spotify. When the Link is activated, the appropriate song or Playlist is automatically available in the application.

Leasey makes it easy for you to open such Links directly, whereupon you can then follow a Playlist or listen to the music track.

When activating either the Context Menu for a track or Playlist, you will see the option “Copy URI”. Press Enter on this. It is then available on the Clipboard, which you can verify by pressing the Leasey Key followed by X. It can then be pasted into a tweet, Email or other text edit environment and sent to someone else for listening.

If on the other hand someone sends you a Spotify U R I, as you are using Leasey you can first copy the U R I to the Clipboard, then press Control+Shift+U, or activate the appropriate option on the Leasey Spotify Menu. An Edit Field is available, with a prompt requesting that you paste the U R I there. Please do this, then press Enter. Spotify will load the appropriate item.

If the U R I points to a Playlist, you will be taken to the page relating to it, whereupon it can be played or followed. Please refer to the earlier section concerning viewing a Playlist page.

If you have been sent a URI for a song, it is likely Spotify will take you to the album on which it appears. Now you have the ability to run a Spotify URI easily, ask your friends to share their Playlists or favourite songs with you, and, enjoy the music!

Choose the Device to Play On

You may care to use your mobile device on which to listen to Spotify. If you have a number of Playlists which you are following, you have a large collection of songs in ‘Your Music’, or you just want to hear songs which can be quickly found using Leasey Spotify, you can hear these on your mobile device. Particularly if you have an external speaker or speakers, this can make for a wonderful listening experience as you can hear your music independent of the computer.

Certainly, the app for Spotify on I O S devices is particularly accessible and indeed using that, it is possible to create Playlists and add tracks to them yourself, then listen to those on the computer if you wish, in a simlar way to that described above.

If you are using Spotify on the computer, and you wish for your mobile device to immediately take over and start playing the music output, follow these steps:

Step 1. Open the Spotify app on your mobile device and ensure it has an internet connection.

Step 2. Using the computer, press Control+End to move to the end of any Spotify page.

Step 3. Press Shift+B to reach the ‘Choose the Device to Play On’ Button.

Step 4. Press Enter.

Step 5. Press down Arrow repeatedly and you should see a list of devices detected, including your computer and the name of your mobile device.

Step 6. Press Enter on the name of your mobile device. It may take a second or two but the audio playback should begin. If it does not, exit ‘Browse Mode’ by pressing F12, then press the Space Bar. All being well, you should hear the music from your mobile device.

If while the mobile device is connected, and you carry out any of the steps described in this Chapter such as playing a song by pressing the Enter key, communication will be sent to your mobile device as this is now the primary source for audio output. This means that all the control of Spotify can be carried out using the computer while you are listening to the music and it is reflected on the mobile device. It’s like magic!

If while browsing any page you press Control+End, you should be able to read the line of text stating that you are listening on a mobile device.

To re-enable your computer as the output source, work through the procedure described above. In summary, select the ‘Choose the Device to Play On’ Button by pressing Enter on it, but this time, select ‘This Computer’ in the list of devices which appears. Assuming a song is playing, playback should cease on the mobile device and you should hear it through the computer’s sound source instead.

Spotify Radio.

Leasey Spotify supports the ability to be able to listen to the SpotifyRadio ‘Genre Stations’. You can select a radio station pertaining to a genre and Spotify will play many songs matching the category.

Step 1. From any page, press Insert+F7 to bring into view the list of Links.

Step 2. Press the letter ‘R’ for ‘Radio’.

Step 3. Press Enter.

Step 4. Press Control+End to move to the end of the page.

Step 5. Press Shift+H to locate ‘Genre Stations’.

Step 6. Press the letter ‘B’ repeatedly in order to move through the genres.

Step 7. Press Enter to select the one you want. You should now begin to hear the radio station.

Step 8. Optionally, press Alt+Control+Windows+T to hear the current song title.

Keystroke Summary.

Find on Spotify, Control+Shift+F.

Find on Spotify via Leasey Search, Control+Shift+S.

Pause and Play Song, Alt+Control+Windows+P.

Volume Up, Control+Windows+Alt+Up Arrow.

Volume Down, Control+Windows+Alt+Down Arrow.

Next Track, Control+Shift+N.

Previous Track, Control+Shift+P.

Fast Forward, Alt+Control+Windows+Right Arrow.

Rewind, Alt+Control+Windows+Left Arrow.

Toggle Shuffle, Control+S.

Toggle Repeat, Control+R.

Paste Spotify U R I, Control+Shift+U.

Studio Recorder

Studio Recorder is a seriously underrated software package from APH, the American Printing House for the Blind, and is ideal for anyone who wishes to record speech perhaps for podcasting, to produce and edit the reading of a book, or some other purpose. While not widely recognised, it also can be used to mix music with speech. Indeed we would go as far as saying that unless you want to use multi-track software, it beats every other mainstream product hands-down for mixing sound on sound for some very compelling reasons! We have a training course available for purchase relating to how to use Studio Recorder.

Some JAWS scripts were created for the training course mentioned above. In addition to providing additional spoken information when visiting some fields within Dialog Boxes, there are some additional utilities.

Ordinarily, pressing the Space Bar will activate the Play and Pause function of Studio Recorder. Pressing Enter will stop the audio playing, relocating the cursor back at the point where play had commenced. However, some people used to working with other audio editors would prefer that pressing the Enter key paused playback. For very precise editing on extremely small fragments of audio this makes the process easier. Should you require this functionality, press Alt+Windows+F12. This is a toggle action and will enable and disable this special setting.

Other keystrokes you may find helpful in Studio Recorder are:

  • To report the current time press Shift+control+M.
  • To report the total file length press Insert+Delete or Caps Lock+Delete if using the laptop layout.
  • To report the selection length press Shift+Insert+Down Arrow.
  • To hear a sound indicating whether recording is in progress press Alt Grave Accent next to number 1 Alt+`.
  • To toggle whether the time is announced when the Enter, Escape or Space Bar is used press Alt+Windows+F11.

Keystroke Summary.

Space Bar: Plays or pauses audio in Studio Recorder.

Enter: Stops audio playback in the default Studio Recorder behaviour.

Alt+Windows+F12: Toggles whether Enter pauses playback instead of stopping and returning to the original cursor position.

Shift+Control+M: Reports the current time.

Insert+Delete: Reports the total file length.

Caps Lock+Delete: Reports the total file length when using the JAWS laptop keyboard layout.

Shift+Insert+Down Arrow: Reports the selection length.

Alt+Grave Accent: Plays a sound indicating whether recording is in progress.

Alt+Windows+F11: Toggles whether the time is announced when Enter, Escape or Space Bar is used.

VLC Media Player and Additional Winamp Functionality

Many people enjoy using Winamp or VLC Media Player. This section discusses the use of VLC and an additional function you can use in conjunction with the Winamp player.

VLC is an extremely widely used player which will handle just about any audio or video file you throw at it. It also gives you the ability to play CD’s and DVD’s if you have a necessary drive attached and that includes audio description content.

First of all, you are going to download VLC Media player. It will not take a degree in computer science to find it. Just google the term, download VLC media player, and you will be there.

Keystrokes and Concepts.

There are many keystrokes in VLC. Leasey interacts with a good many of them so as not to provide conflict with JAWS native commands and also to ensure that in certain conditions it speaks or sends to Braille appropriate information. You can activate or deactivate “Verbosity Mode” by pressing Control+Shift+V. When enabled, this mode will announce additional information, such as the file name when you move to the next track, the cursor position as you move through the item, etc.

So first of all, we will load a folder into VLC. You can do this by pressing Control+F. If you want to open a file it is Control+O, or of course you can just launch it from File Explorer. CTRL + D : Opens disk, such as a DVD

The first item begins to play. Here are some keystrokes you may care to use.

  • Space equals Play and Pause.
  • Control+Up and Down Arrow will change the volume level.
  • N moves to the next track.
  • P moves to the previous track.
  • S stops item from playing.
  • Left bracket next to P: Decrease playing speed. If verbosity is on, speedh is announced.
  • Right bracket: Increase playing speed. If verbosity is on, speedh is announced.
  • Left and Right Arrow: 10 seconds forward or back.
  • Shift with Left and Right Arrow: 3 seconds forward or back.
  • CTRL + RIGHT or Left ARROW : 1 minute forward or back.
  • Alt+Shift+T: Announce elapsed time.
  • Shift+Control+T: Announce remaining time.
  • Alt+Control+T: Announce total time.
  • B: Cycle through available audio tracks, for example on a DVD.
  • M: Mute sound on and off.
  • Shift+A: cycles through all the audio devices available.
  • Control+L: switch to playlist or back to media.
  • Control+T Go to Time. Listen to the instructions provided and type the format exactly as described.
  • Control+V followed by Enter, launch a specific URL. This can be a YouTube video, SoundCloud audio, radio station and so on. If you have the URL for a video or audio source you can use that too.
  • Alternatively, you can press Control+N to open a network stream, paste it in and press Enter.

Locating a Previously Saved Position in Winamp or VLC.

You may well be interested in hearing audio books in MP3 format or similar. In this event, you may wish at a later time to pick up from the point where you left off reading.

Step 1. Pause the playback of the book by pressing the Space Bar.

Step 2. Close the program down by pressing Alt+F4 in the usual way.

Step 3. Open up the file again at a later time and it will begin playback.

Step 4. Press Alt+Windows+K so as to move back to the previously stored position.

Please note that the storing of the saved position is file specific, that is to say that the position is retained relative to the file you were previously playing.

Setting And Locating Bookmarks in VLC.

It is possible to set bookmarks in VLC Media Player so as to return to strategic points within the audio at a later time.

Step 1. Locate the point in the file where you wish to set the bookmark.

Step 2. Press the Leasey Key then Control+1.

Step 3. Type a name for the bookmark and press Enter.

Step 4. To locate a bookmark, press the Leasey Key then 1. A list of bookmarks relative to the current file is available. Select the one you wish to move to and press Enter. The audio should then begin playing at the desired location.

Step 5. To delete a bookmark, press the Leasey Key then 2. A list of bookmarks relative to the current file is available. Select the one you wish to remove and press Enter.

Keystroke Summary.

Play or Pause, Space.

Volume Up or Down, Up or Down Arrow.

Mute or unmute audio, M.

Open folder, Control+F.

Open file, Control+O.

Open disk, Control+D.

Next track, N.

Previous track, P.

Stop track, S.

Increase speed, Right Bracket.

Decrease speed, Left bracket.

Say speed, Control+Shift+S.

10 Seconds back or Forward, Left and Right Arrow.

3 Seconds back or forward, Shift+Left and Right Arrow.

1 Minute back or forward, Control+Left and Right Arrow.

Say elapsed time, Alt+Shift+T.

Say remaining time, Control+Shift+T.

Say total time, Control+Alt+T.

Cycle through available audio tracks on disk, B.

Cycle through audio sources available, Shift+A.

Switch from media window to playlist view, Control+L.

Go to time, Control+T.

Launch source if you have the URL, Control+V then Enter.

Open network stream, Control+N, Control+V then Enter.

Relocate stop time of previous playback, Alt+Windows+K.

Set a bookmark, Leasey Key then Control+1.

Choose a bookmark from a list, Leasey Key then 1.

Delete a bookmark from a list, Leasey Key then 2.

Organizing information

Leasey Alerts

Introduction.

Have you ever been confronted with a situation where you’ve been to a website, and you always want to come back to the same place if it exists each time you visit it? Google would be a very good example, When you’ve searched for something, and the new page loads, you do not want to have to find where the search results start.

A Leasey Alert will not only advise you that the text exists, but it will also set focus to the relevant area of the page. All you need do is set up the Leasey Alert and then forget about it, unless you want to delete it.

Setting a Leasey Alert.

Please note: while examples of Leasey Alert creation and usage are given in relation to individual web sites, it is more than possible that the content of the web sites concerned will have changed following publication of this User Guide. The examples given therefore are just that: mere examples of hypothetical situations which will need to be adapted according to the individual web sites being used.

We will first create a Leasey Alert to set focus to the Search results on Google.

Step 1. Visit www.google.co.uk or www.google.com.
